avatar-decorator.name: Avatar Decorator
avatar-decorator.description: Add V badges, gradient borders and cute accessories to your avatar in one click. Stand out from the crowd with easy export.

seo.intro: Avatar Decorator is a free in-browser profile picture decoration tool that overlays verified-style badges, gradient circular borders, decorative corner pins, seasonal frames, and circle or hexagon mask shapes onto any square selfie photo — entirely in the browser and without sending the image to a server. Upload a profile photo then layer on a blue Twitter/X-style V verified badge, gold creator badge, round gradient frames, holiday borders, and emoji or accessory stickers. All compositing runs client-side through pure Canvas, so the original headshot never leaves your device, no signup is required, and no watermark is added to the exported PNG.
scenarios: Adding a clean blue verified V badge or Xiaohongshu-style creator badge to a personal headshot for self-branding without uploading the private photo to an online editor
Framing a work or class team avatar with Lunar New Year or holiday seasonal borders and pin stickers before a seasonal social media rebrand
Converting a square selfie into a circle, hexagon, rounded-square, or framed hexagon mask shape for a consistent WeChat, QQ, Instagram, or LinkedIn profile crop
tutorial: Upload a square or rectangular profile picture by clicking the file picker or dragging the image into the dropzone; the tool auto-centers and auto-scales it to a square canvas
Pick a mask shape: clean circle, hexagon, rounded-square, or keep the original square shape with uniform border padding
Select a verified badge (blue V, gold creator, or custom color) and add gradient circular borders, corner frames, pins, and seasonal stickers by dragging them anywhere on the canvas
Download the decorated avatar as a transparent PNG and upload directly to the social platform's profile picture change form
advantages: Pure in-browser Canvas rendering with zero uploads, so private headshots, personal photos, and professional creator portraits never leave the editing machine
Covers the top profile decoration workflows: verified badges, seasonal frames, and non-square mask shapes — all in one tool instead of three separate editors
Exports a 1080x1080 square PNG that works as a profile picture for every major Chinese and Western social site, so one export fits WeChat, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and QQ

faqs.q: Will my original profile photo be uploaded to any server to add these decorations?
faqs.a: No. Every composite step, frame render, badge overlay, and mask cut happens inside your browser through the HTML5 Canvas API. No image bytes, no metadata, no photo pixels are sent or cached anywhere by the tool or a third party — your original photo stays on your device end-to-end.

faqs.q: Which social platforms does the exported avatar size and shape work for?
faqs.a: The default export is a 1080x1080 square PNG, which is the universal safe avatar size that works natively on Xiaohongshu, WeChat Moments, Weibo, QQ, Line, Douyin, Twitter/X, Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn profiles. Each platform will auto-center the PNG, so nothing important gets cropped out unexpectedly.

faqs.q: Can I add a verified-style V badge to any photo for free and without a watermark?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose a blue verified V, gold creator-style badge, or a custom-colored badge. The badge defaults to the bottom-right corner but is manually draggable anywhere on the canvas. The exported PNG preserves badge transparency, and no site watermark is applied anywhere on the final avatar.

faqs.q: What mask shapes, borders, and decorative accessories does the tool support?
faqs.a: Supported masks include clean circle, hexagon, rounded-square, sharp square, and uniform-padding frames. Border options include gradient ring frames, thin/thick solid-color rings, and corner-only partial borders. Decorative accessories span emoji pins, flower corner pins, graduation caps, and holiday stickers for Christmas, Lunar New Year, and Valentine's seasons.

faqs.q: Can I save a decorated avatar draft and come back to tweak it later?
faqs.a: Your current decoration state stays in the page session for the same open tab, so repositioning pins or swapping badge colors works within one session. After you refresh or close the tab, the state resets — for long-term reuse, we recommend downloading the final PNG and re-uploading it into the tool if you want to add extra layers on top later.

base64-tool.name: Base64 Encoder/Decoder
base64-tool.description: Online Base64 encoding and decoding with text↔image conversion. Fully local processing for safety and privacy.

seo.intro: This Base64 encoder and decoder converts text and files to and from Base64 directly in your browser. Encode UTF-8 text without garbled characters, decode a Base64 string back to readable text, or turn a small image into a data URI you can embed in HTML or CSS. Because it runs locally, nothing you paste or upload is sent to a server. It's a quick helper for developers working with APIs, config files and inline assets.
scenarios: Turn a small icon or image into a data URI to embed it inline in CSS or HTML.
Inspect or decode a Base64 field returned by an API or stored in a token.
Encode text containing special characters so it survives transport safely.
tutorial: Choose encode or decode.
Paste your text, or select a file such as an image.
Confirm UTF-8 so non-ASCII characters are handled correctly.
Copy the encoded string or the decoded result.
advantages: Handles both text and files, including image-to-data-URI.
UTF-8 aware, so Chinese and other non-ASCII text won't be corrupted.
Processes locally in the browser — your data is never uploaded.

faqs.q: Does it support non-ASCII text like Chinese?
faqs.a: Yes. It encodes and decodes as UTF-8, so multilingual text is preserved without garbled output.

faqs.q: Can it convert an image to Base64?
faqs.a: Yes. Select an image file and it returns a Base64 string or data URI you can embed directly in your markup.

faqs.q: Is there a size limit?
faqs.a: There's no hard limit, but large files depend on your browser's memory since encoding happens locally.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Base64 and URL encoding?
faqs.a: Base64 represents binary data as ASCII text; URL (percent) encoding escapes characters that are unsafe in URLs. They solve different problems.

faqs.q: Is my data uploaded?
faqs.a: No. Encoding and decoding run entirely in your browser, so nothing leaves your device.

caption-generator.name: Social Captions
caption-generator.description: Beat writer's block! 8 categories including travel, food, romance and work. Hundreds of handpicked captions, one-click copy.

seo.intro: Social Captions Generator is a free online idea board for copy-ready social media posts across travel, food, romance, work, motivation, and lifestyle themes. Browse hundreds of hand-curated one-liners, captions, and quotes grouped by mood and use case, then copy your favorite with one click for WeChat Moments, Instagram, TikTok, or Xiaohongshu. All captions ship with the browser page — no subscription, no writer's-block prompts, and no network call is needed to fetch or search the library.
scenarios: Beating writer's block before posting a restaurant review, travel photo dump, or couple shoot to Xiaohongshu or Instagram
Picking a soft, playful, or aesthetic caption for a WeChat Moments update so the post matches the tone of the photos
Curating batch captions for a brand's social calendar or influencer content queue so posts don't all sound generic
tutorial: Open the category that matches your post theme — travel, food, date, work, motivation, fitness, lifestyle, or pet
Browse the card list or type a keyword into the filter bar to narrow down to a specific tone (funny, soft, sassy, short)
Click any caption card to copy it to the clipboard immediately
Paste into your social app and optionally tweak a few words or emojis so it reads like your own voice
advantages: Curated by copywriters instead of auto-generated, so captions avoid the generic AI-wash sound and fit actual platform usage patterns
Covers 8+ mood and topic buckets with hundreds of cards, so there's a usable line even for niche post ideas like gym selfies, study sessions, or weekend brunch
One-click copy plus fast keyword filtering means no typing and no extra prompts — perfect for creators posting several times a day

faqs.q: Are these captions AI-generated or written by human copywriters?
faqs.a: The core library is curated and edited by copywriters, with only light cleanup formatting passes — no bulk LLM dumps. Cards are sorted by platform usage patterns so the top options are phrasing that actually performs on WeChat Moments, Instagram, and Xiaohongshu rather than generic templates.

faqs.q: Which social platforms do these captions work best for?
faqs.a: They are written for WeChat Moments (朋友圈), Xiaohongshu, Instagram, TikTok captions, and generic microblogging. The lengths cover both the short 'one-line mood' style and the slightly longer paragraph form common on lifestyle platforms, with hashtag-ready variations included in several categories.

faqs.q: Can I search by tone or keyword instead of scrolling categories?
faqs.a: Yes. A built-in keyword filter lets you type words like 'funny', 'travel', 'food', 'selfie', 'sad', or 'aesthetic' to surface cards across all categories, useful when you know the vibe but don't yet know the exact bucket you want.

faqs.q: Do I need to sign up or pay to access the full library?
faqs.a: No. Every card loads in the page at open time, and one-click copy works without signup, login, or a paywall. There is no rate limit on copying, either, so teams can batch-prepare a social queue quickly.

faqs.q: Will every single caption fit my photo perfectly out of the box?
faqs.a: Captions are inspiration starters with a proven structure. For a perfect post, we recommend pasting the one you like, then swapping the city name, restaurant, or photo detail for the real specifics of your own shot — the built-in Text Toolbox on the same site makes final tweaks fast.

case-converter.name: Case Converter — Convert Text Case Online
case-converter.description: Convert text between 10+ case formats: UPPER, lower, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, Title Case and more. Free, instant, no signup.

seo.intro: This case converter transforms text between UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, and programming styles like camelCase and snake_case. Paste your text, pick the target format, and copy the result. It preserves line breaks so you can convert whole lists at once, which is useful for cleaning up headings, normalising imported data, or renaming variables. It works entirely in your browser.
scenarios: Normalise a set of headings to consistent Title Case.
Convert variable names between camelCase and snake_case while coding.
Clean up imported data where capitalisation is inconsistent across rows.
tutorial: Paste your text, one item per line if converting a list.
Choose the target format such as UPPERCASE, Title Case or snake_case.
Apply the conversion.
Copy the converted text.
advantages: Includes programming naming styles (camelCase, snake_case), not just upper/lower.
Keeps line breaks so you can batch-convert multiple lines.
Runs client-side with no upload.

faqs.q: Does it support camelCase and snake_case?
faqs.a: Yes. Besides UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case and Sentence case, it converts to programming styles like camelCase and snake_case.

faqs.q: Does Title Case skip small words?
faqs.a: Title Case capitalises the first letter of words; simple implementations capitalise every word, so review short words like 'of' or 'the' if you need strict style rules.

faqs.q: Does it work with non-Latin text like Chinese?
faqs.a: Case conversion only affects letters that have upper/lower forms. Chinese characters have no case, so they pass through unchanged.

faqs.q: Is there a character limit?
faqs.a: There's no hard limit; large blocks of text are processed locally in your browser.

faqs.q: Can I convert multiple lines at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Line breaks are preserved, so paste a list and every line is converted together.

color-picker.name: Color Picker
color-picker.description: Free online color picker with eyedropper, HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV/CMYK conversion, color palette generator, gradient builder, contrast checker (WCAG AA/AAA) and...

seo.intro: Color Picker is a free online color tool that lets you pick, convert, and combine colors from a single visual workspace. Move an eyedropper across a palette, paste any HEX, RGB, HSL, or HSV code to see its matches, build multi-stop gradients, and export curated palettes ready for CSS, design tools, or brand guidelines. All conversion and rendering happens locally in your browser — brand colors and client artwork values never touch a server.
scenarios: Sampling colors from a design reference or uploaded image and translating them into HEX values for CSS or a Figma library
Tuning a landing page palette by adjusting saturation, luminance, and contrast between brand and accent colors
Generating a multi-stop linear or radial gradient and copying its CSS snippet into a website or ad banner
tutorial: Select a starting color using the picker canvas, eyedropper, or by pasting a HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV code into the input
Toggle between color model tabs to copy the equivalent value in the format your workflow needs
Build a palette or gradient by adding swatches and adjusting stop positions and easing curves
Copy the final CSS string, PNG preview, or shareable palette link for your design or codebase
advantages: Full HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV round-tripping with alpha support, so moving between CSS, Swift/Kotlin mobile code, and design tools never loses precision
Live gradient builder with CSS output and real-time preview, so you can iterate to the exact look before pasting into production
All math runs in-browser; brand color values and uploaded reference images are never sent or indexed anywhere

faqs.q: Can I convert between HEX, RGB, HSL, and HSV without losing precision?
faqs.a: Yes. Every conversion uses the standard sRGB color space math and keeps the alpha channel intact. You can round-trip the same color between all four formats and back to the original code as many times as you want without drift.

faqs.q: Does the picker support opacity / alpha values for translucent UI elements?
faqs.a: Yes. Each color model exposes a dedicated alpha slider, and the output formats include 8-digit HEX with alpha, rgba(), hsla(), and hsva() so the code you paste matches exactly what design tools and browsers expect.

faqs.q: If I drop an image into the eyedropper, is that image uploaded to your servers?
faqs.a: No. The image is decoded and drawn onto an in-memory canvas inside your browser. No pixel data, palette, or file blob leaves your device, so brand assets, client moodboards, and confidential UI mockups stay private.

faqs.q: Can I save or share a palette or gradient with a teammate?
faqs.a: Yes. The share URL embeds the full palette or gradient state in the hash so anyone with the link sees the exact same colors, and you can also export the palette as plain text, CSS variables, or an image preview for a brand deck.

faqs.q: How do I make sure two text-on-background colors meet WCAG contrast rules?
faqs.a: The contrast panel computes the ratio between any foreground swatch and the background color in real time and flags whether the pair passes AA, AAA, or the large-text threshold, letting you adjust hue and saturation until the pair is accessible.

copy-cleaner.name: Copy Redundancy Cleaner & Annotator
copy-cleaner.description: Local parse only. Auto detect repetitive preambles, meaningless adjectives, repeated golden lines, filler nonsense. Colored highlight redundant segments,...

seo.intro: Copy Redundancy Cleaner & Annotator is a free in-browser text tool for Xiaohongshu, WeChat Official, short-video voiceover, and e-commerce PDP copy operators. Paste your raw draft, and the tool automatically finds redundant fluff (double intensifiers like 'very very', repeated phrasing, empty marketing filler), absolute-expression risk words, and over-long sentences, then outputs a compressed version, line-by-line replacement suggestions, and per-sentence scores, typically cutting 20%–50% of characters without changing meaning — perfect for squeezing a wordy first draft into platform-sized short copy.
scenarios: A Xiaohongshu influencer writes an 800-character first draft that is too verbose. Runs it through Cleaner to strip filler and duplicated adjectives, shrinks it below 500 characters, then splits with emoji and paragraphs into the platform-ideal 3–4 screen read length

An e-commerce PDP draft ran 4 pages long. Operator runs Cleaner to flag 12 repeated selling points and 8 absolute-clause risk words ('top / ultimate / one of a kind'), then sends the compressed version for legal review — fewer compliance issues plus the whole pitch fits in 1.5 screens

A 3-minute short-video voiceover script is too long for the slot. Cleaner auto-compresses to the selected intensity, freeing speaking room for emotion and pauses; the resulting tight draft fits exactly in 55 seconds without manual sentence-by-sentence deletion
tutorial: Paste the copy to clean in the main input. Chinese, English, line breaks, bullet lists, dialogue formats all work. Thousands of characters process fine since everything runs in browser locally.

Choose cleanup intensity: Light removes duplicates and obvious filler; Medium strips empty filler and redundant adjectives; High also compresses long sentences and gently reorders wording for tighter copy — bigger character reduction with readability preserved.

Review three output panes: annotated view (red = redundant, yellow = risky, green = suggestion), compressed dry copy, per-sentence scores and replacements. Click any sentence's keep / replace button to edit only that sentence and leave the rest untouched.
Pick an export format: plain compressed text, annotated HTML for team review, or side-by-side dual-column Markdown. Paste directly into CapCut copy, WeChat editor, or Xiaohongshu publish screen.
advantages: Triple filtering in one tool: redundancy / repeated words + empty-marketing-filler scoring + China Ad Law absolute-risk-word flagging. Solves both 'my copy is too wordy' and 'is this legally risky' pain points with a single paste, not just a plain deduper.

Sentence-level locking: if you want to keep a punchline, slogan, or selling line, mark it locked before compression and Cleaner will never touch it, so your intentionally designed lines never get deleted as 'filler'.

100% browser-local, zero upload. Unreleased brand slogans, confidential upcoming product PDP copy, and private contracted influencer drafts are safe pasted straight in. All regex matching and compression runs in client-side JavaScript with no backend storage.

faqs.q: Does it automatically change the meaning? Will aggressive compression delete selling points?
faqs.a: By default all compression is 'meaning-preserving trim': it only removes repeats, empty modifiers, absolute adverbs, and synonymous duplicates — it never changes stated facts, core selling points, or brand names. Only High intensity lightly reorders syntax, and even then it locks proper nouns, numbers, dates, and brand tokens. You can also lock any specific key sentence to force it untouched.

faqs.q: Does it flag Ad Law risk words like 'national-level' or 'best'?
faqs.a: Yes. Chinese mode ships a built-in dictionary of common Ad Law absolute words ('best / only / number one / ultimate / top-tier' etc.) and shows in-context replacement suggestions — e.g. swap 'the absolute best' for 'one of my favorite picks I have used', 'lowest price on the web' for 'promotional price during the event' — compliant while keeping sales tone.

faqs.q: Does it support English copy? Can I use it for cross-border Amazon listings?
faqs.a: Yes. English Cleaner ships its own library for repeated intensifiers ('very very', 'absolutely absolutely'), marketing fluff ('game-changing', 'revolutionary'), and Amazon red-flag absolute words ('#1', 'best in the world'). It works well on 5-point bullet PDPs, A+ copy, and ad lines, though replacement suggestions are currently Chinese-first — English synonym banks will grow with updates.

faqs.q: Can it process long copy of thousands of characters, or only ~200 char blobs?
faqs.a: Thousands of characters work totally fine. Everything runs browser-local; internal tests clean + annotate + compress a 5000-character WeChat long article in 1–2 seconds without backend calls. It only chokes on novel-length 100k+ inputs which are not the intended use case.

faqs.q: Does output preserve formatting like lists and headings?
faqs.a: Yes. Cleaning and compression preserves Markdown headings, bullet lists, bold, and italic markers — it never melts headings and paragraphs into one plain text blob. Markdown and HTML exports keep all structure, so you can paste into WeChat editors or Notion with almost no layout retouch.

countdown.name: Countdown & Anniversary
countdown.description: Track important dates with real-time second-accurate countdowns. Never miss a birthday, holiday or anniversary. Supports yearly repeats.

seo.intro: This online countdown timer counts down to a target date and time, or for a set duration, and displays the remaining days, hours, minutes and seconds. Set your target, start it, and optionally switch to a large full-screen view for events, launches, exams or livestreams. It runs in your browser with no account required, so you can spin one up in seconds.
scenarios: Build hype for a product launch, sale or webinar with a live countdown.
Track a deadline, exam date or project due date at a glance.
Show a 'starting soon' countdown before a livestream or presentation begins.
tutorial: Set the target date and time, or a fixed duration.
Choose a display style and, if you want, full-screen mode.
Press start to begin the countdown.
When it reaches zero, the timer shows it has finished.
advantages: Large, readable full-screen display suited to presentations and streams.
No sign-up needed — set it and go.
Runs client-side, so it works even on a simple shared screen.

faqs.q: Will it keep counting if I close the page?
faqs.a: The timer runs while the page is open. If you close or reload the tab, re-open it and the remaining time to a fixed target date will recalculate automatically.

faqs.q: Can I show it full screen?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to full-screen mode for a large display that's easy to read from a distance on a projector or stream.

faqs.q: Is there a sound alert when it ends?
faqs.a: When the countdown reaches zero the display updates to a finished state; sound depends on the selected style and your browser's autoplay settings.

faqs.q: Can I run more than one countdown?
faqs.a: Each open tab runs its own countdown, so you can open the tool in several tabs for multiple timers.

faqs.q: Does it work on mobile?
faqs.a: Yes. It's responsive and works in mobile browsers, though keeping the screen awake depends on your device settings.

danmaku.name: Handheld LED Banner
danmaku.description: Turn your phone into a scrolling LED banner. Perfect for concerts, airport pickups and fan cheering. Multiple colors & scroll speeds.

seo.intro: Danmaku Handheld is a free browser tool that turns any Chinese, English, or emoji text into a horizontally scrolling LED-style marquee you can hold up on your phone like a portable light sign at concerts, fan meetups, airport pickups, or clubs. Pick text color, font size, scroll speed, background, toggle full-screen, and turn phone brightness to maximum — no app install, no account registration.
scenarios: At a K-pop, C-pop concert or outdoor music festival, front-row fans hold up phones showing idol names, slogans, and official fan colors as a low-cost alternative to dedicated physical LED light sticks

Picking someone up at the airport or train station: display their name plus flight or train number in a large high-contrast yellow-on-black marquee so they can spot you far away without a paper sign that blows away
At clubs, murder-mystery parties, or team-building icebreakers, send interactive lines to friends' phones as scrolling text for atmosphere instead of printed paper cards.
tutorial: Type the text to show in the top input. Chinese, English, numbers, and emoji can be freely mixed. Keep each line under a few dozen characters; split very long slogans into multiple paragraphs.
Pick text and background colors. Use fan colors for concerts, high-contrast yellow on black for airports, neon hues for clubs.
Use sliders to tune font size and scroll speed. For distant concert visibility use max size and slow speed; for crowded airport pickup use medium settings. The preview updates in real time.
Press full-screen to hide browser chrome, turn the phone horizontally, and set brightness to maximum. For very long displays plug in a charger and turn off auto screen lock.
advantages: True full-screen horizontal LED-style scrolling on phones, tablets, and desktops with no address bar or buttons visible on stage — visually reads like a dedicated LED sign, not a random phone screen.
Fine-grained controls: font size, speed, weight, letter spacing, direction, solid or gradient background, blink mode — one tool covers concerts, pickups, clubs, weddings, and playful use cases.
100% browser-local, no install, no signup, no location or camera permissions. Works offline after first page load, which is safer at security-checked large event venues.

faqs.q: Will it work at venues with no mobile signal?
faqs.a: Yes. Every rendering step runs in client-side JavaScript; there are zero backend API calls. Open the page once while on Wi-Fi, and it keeps working in flight mode or dead zones. Preload the page before leaving home to be safe.

faqs.q: Can leaving my phone at max brightness cause OLED burn-in?
faqs.a: Normal LCD phones are usually fine. If you have an OLED or AMOLED phone (Samsung, many Chinese flagships), leaving a static bright line for many hours does carry mild burn-in risk. Turn the screen off for 10 seconds every 2 minutes, or turn on the built-in anti-burn slow-drift mode that shifts text slightly over time.

faqs.q: Can I show two lines or mix flags and emoji with text?
faqs.a: Yes. Press Enter in the input to create multi-line text. All Unicode emoji, flags, hearts, stars, and custom glyphs render normally. Chinese combined with idol names plus emoji is a fan favorite for high on-stage readability.

faqs.q: Can I export it as a GIF or video for social media?
faqs.a: This version focuses on live handheld display. For social posts, use your phone's built-in screen recorder and capture 10 seconds of the full-screen scroll; it preserves all the colors and speed tuning you configured.

faqs.q: Can the background be transparent for compositing over photos as a sticker?
faqs.a: Yes. Flip background to transparent mode and only the text layer renders. You can then use browser devtools to screenshot a clean text PNG or layer it on other assets. Opaque solid colors read better at live events, but transparency is excellent for secondary design work.

decision-wheel.name: Decision Wheel
decision-wheel.description: Say goodbye to decision fatigue! Let the wheel decide what to eat for lunch, where to go on weekends — just give it a spin.

seo.intro: This spinning decision wheel makes a random choice from a list of options you enter. Type in names, tasks or ideas, spin the wheel, and it lands on one at random — great for breaking decision paralysis, picking a winner, or choosing who goes next. It's visual and fun, works with no sign-up, and runs entirely in your browser so you can use it live on a shared screen or stream.
scenarios: Draw a name for turn-taking, chores or team stand-ups.
Settle 'what should we eat' or any either-or choice when nobody can decide.
Pick a giveaway winner live during a stream or class.
tutorial: Enter your options, one per line.
Spin the wheel.
Read the option it lands on.
Spin again, or remove the picked option to draw without repeats.
advantages: Visual spinning wheel that's engaging for live audiences.
No sign-up — enter options and spin immediately.
Runs client-side, so it works on a projector, shared screen or stream.

faqs.q: How many options can I add?
faqs.a: You can add many; the wheel stays readable with a moderate list, and very large lists simply show thinner segments.

faqs.q: Is the result truly random and fair?
faqs.a: Yes. Each spin uses the browser's random number generator, giving every option an equal chance unless you set weights.

faqs.q: Can I set weights so some options win more?
faqs.a: If weighting is enabled, you can make certain options larger; otherwise every option has an equal probability.

faqs.q: Can I save my options?
faqs.a: Options stay while the page is open. To reuse a list later, keep it in a note and paste it back in.

faqs.q: Does it work on mobile?
faqs.a: Yes. The wheel is touch-friendly and spins in mobile browsers, so you can use it on a phone or tablet.

emoji-mixer.name: Emoji Mixer — Combine & Create New Emojis
emoji-mixer.description: Blend any two emojis into a unique hybrid sticker. Real-time Canvas rendering, transparent PNG export. Perfect for social media, chats, and custom...

seo.intro: Emoji Mixer is a free fun in-browser creative tool that combines two standard emojis into a brand-new blended hybrid emoji sticker you can share as a transparent PNG. Pick any two emojis from the built-in picker — for example cat + 🎂 cake or 🐶 dog + 🚀 rocket — and the mixer will render a fused hybrid emoji mashup combining colors, shapes, and iconography of both inputs. The whole render happens client-side in Canvas, so no sign-in or upload needed and every new mashup is generated instantly right in the page.
scenarios: Creating original hybrid emoji stickers for a Xiaohongshu comment, WeChat group chat, or Discord server so the reaction feels one-of-a-kind instead of the default emoji library
Designing custom fun stickers or branding marks for a personal brand or newsletter by blending industry-relevant emojis (coffee + document for a writer blog, for instance)
Playing a creative icebreaker at a remote team or classroom activity: each person blends two emojis that describe their week, then shares the resulting PNG sticker in the team chat
tutorial: Open the emoji picker for Slot A and pick your first emoji — anything from the full standard Unicode list works (animals, food, objects, faces, symbols)
Pick your second emoji from Slot B's picker; you can swap A and B with one tap to quickly try the reverse blend
Hit the Blend/Mix button and wait a split second for the Canvas renderer to fuse the two inputs into a hybrid mashup
Click the Copy Sticker or Download PNG button to grab the transparent-background hybrid and paste it directly into a chat, notes doc, or social post
advantages: Full emoji library client-side rendered: every standard Unicode emoji on your device can be mixed with zero server calls, no downloads, and no paid credits
Instant generation — clicking the Blend button shows the result in under a second in normal cases; no waiting in a queue for an AI job or loading spinners on slow connections
Outputs a clean transparent PNG sticker that works natively in WeChat custom sticker uploads, Xiaohongshu image comments, iMessage, WhatsApp, Discord, and almost every modern chat and notes app

faqs.q: How does the Emoji Mixer combine two emojis — is it an AI draw?
faqs.a: The mixer combines two standard emojis using your device's native emoji font + color blending, color averaging, and shape composite rules inside the HTML5 Canvas API; it does not call a remote generative AI model. That's why results appear instantly and there is no network dependency or paid token requirement.

faqs.q: Can I mix ANY two emojis or only some preset pairs?
faqs.a: You can mix literally any two standard Unicode emojis that render on your device: animals, faces, flags, food, vehicles, symbols, and objects all work. The picker lists hundreds of categorized emojis, but you can also paste emojis from your keyboard directly. Order matters — picking A=🐶 dog + B=🚀 rocket will look different from A=rocket + B=dog because the blend weights the base shape vs. accent overlay differently.

faqs.q: What file format is the hybrid emoji exported in and will it have a white background?
faqs.a: Every blend exports as a standard RGBA PNG with full alpha transparency so the sticker sits cleanly on any chat bubble color, dark mode, or light mode background without a white box. There is no watermark, no overlay logo, and no metadata added to the final PNG file.

faqs.q: Will I get the exact same blend result if two different people mix the same emoji pair?
faqs.a: Blend results depend slightly on your device and browser's native system emoji font (Apple Color Emoji on macOS/iOS, Segoe UI Emoji on Windows, Noto Color Emoji on Android, etc.). The exact color palette and shape outline will match the local font, so two Windows PCs will produce identical outputs but an iPhone and Windows PC may have minor visual differences due to their default emoji font vendors.

faqs.q: Can I use the blended hybrid emojis commercially or on branded materials?
faqs.a: Yes for the arrangement and blend output you create — the mixer does not add any proprietary artwork or licensed glyphs; it composites standard Unicode emojis available on your own device. If you intend to use the output on registered trademarks or commercial merchandise, we recommend double-checking that any specific emoji glyph used is acceptable for your jurisdiction's fair-use / trademark rules just as you would with a normal emoji.

fortune-sticks.name: Fortune Sticks
fortune-sticks.description: Draw fortune sticks, yes/no decisions or custom options — the cure for indecision. Three modes, fun and practical.

seo.intro: Fortune Sticks is a free random-decision web tool that recreates the tactile feel of shaking a temple qian'chou fortune tube: click the shake button or physically shake your phone for haptic vibration, then one random stick falls out of the pool, showing the stick number, fortune rank (top-top, top, middle, down, down-down), classic poem, and plain-language explanation. You can also switch to a custom pool to solve trivial everyday choices like restaurants, gifts, or errands.
scenarios: At lunchtime a four-person team is stuck between six restaurants. Paste the six names into a custom pool, shake once, and everyone agrees to obey the result — saves 20 minutes of useless debate

When a couple or close friends are in a petty fight, create a custom pool like 'apologize first', 'buy boba tea as apology', 'silent treatment 2 hours' and shake. The ritual-loaded mini-game avoids emotional escalation because the 'tube decided', not either person

Trip planning indecision: which three Disney rides to hit first, which of two nearby day-trip cities to visit this weekend. Adding the good-omen ritual layer makes everyday random decisions feel more fun instead of tedious.
tutorial: By default it uses a built-in 100-stick temple fortune pool. Switch to custom pool mode and paste your own choices one per line — restaurant names, activities, gifts, chores — whatever you are stuck on.
Click the central SHAKE button or physically shake a vibration-enabled phone. Watch the sticks rattle inside the tube until one falls and settles.
Temple mode shows stick number, fortune grade, poem, plain explanation. Custom pool mode simply reveals the randomly chosen line of text.
Press 'shake again' for another draw, or 'reset / clear' to start over. Any result can be copied to clipboard or exported as a PNG screenshot to share in group chats.
advantages: Dual-mode in one tool: authentic 100-stick temple fortune system with classic Chinese grading plus custom pool mode. Use temple mode for cultural good-omen vibe, custom pool for actually solving choices.

Real phone-shake trigger + haptic vibration + 3D drop animation feels way more engaging than a plain random string generator. At team dinner people actually fight to shake the phone; the ritual creates a shared mini-game.
Custom pools can be exported / imported as JSON, so your signature 'daily slacking tasks' or 'couple make-up actions' pool can be shared with friends instead of retyping 30 options every time.

faqs.q: Is the result actually accurate or just pure randomness?
faqs.a: Under the hood it uses the browser's Math.random plus extra crypto entropy, so mathematically it is uniform distribution. Accuracy depends on personal belief. The big difference from a generic random picker is the cultural shell — temple grades + classic poems make results psychologically easier to accept, especially when picking restaurants to avoid arguments.

faqs.q: How many options fit in a custom pool?
faqs.a: There is no hard upper limit; hundreds of one-line options still run smoothly in internal tests. 5–10 for restaurants, 15 for trip itineraries is the sweet spot. If you go above 100, export a JSON backup first so you don't lose the pool if you close the tab.

faqs.q: What if I draw a 'down-down' fortune, that feels unlucky?
faqs.a: It is all random numbers. If you want psychological comfort: (1) switch to custom mode and remove bad-grade sticks, (2) turn on the optional 'auto-retry once on down-down' switch (off by default), or (3) read the explanation — it always gives actionable plain advice like 'lay low this week' rather than something scary.

faqs.q: Can I export the draw as an image for group chats?
faqs.a: Yes. One-click PNG export of the whole stick card. A long image with number, grade, and poem creates way better team atmosphere than plain text for dinner or trip decisions, and leaves written proof in chat history — 'you were the one who drew hot pot'.

faqs.q: Does the tool record any draw results on a backend?
faqs.a: Never. All draw logic, custom pool text, and PNG rendering run entirely in client-side JavaScript. Not a single byte is sent to a server. Your choices, your custom text, your drawn outcome — nobody including site operators can see them, so it is safe even for emotional or slightly sensitive work and personal decisions.

grid-cutter.name: 9-Grid Photo Cutter
grid-cutter.description: Slice any picture into 9 tiles in one click — perfect for grid posts on social media. Auto square crop, HD output, ordered save.

seo.intro: 9-Grid Photo Cutter is a free in-browser image slicer that splits any square, portrait, or landscape photo into a 3×3 grid of perfectly aligned tiles ready for Xiaohongshu (小红书), Instagram, or WeChat Moments carousels and grid posts. Pick a photo from your device, choose between strict square crop, padding-to-square, or bordered white-border tile export, and download all 9 tiles as individual PNG or JPG files in one zip. Every pixel operation runs in the browser via Canvas — the original photo never leaves your machine and no image data is uploaded or stored anywhere.
scenarios: Turning a travel panorama or group selfie into a 9-tile Xiaohongshu grid post so the full picture cascades across nine consecutive posts on the profile page
Slicing a product launch poster into 3×3 for an Instagram grid puzzle feed so followers land on a cohesive hero visual instead of a disjointed single tiles
Preparing 9 bordered tiles with matching white padding for a WeChat Moments 9-pic upload so each frame stays perfectly square on any screen size
tutorial: Upload a photo from your phone or computer gallery by tapping the file picker or dropping the image into the dropzone
Choose the output shape: hard 1:1 crop, fit-and-pad to make non-square shots, or keep aspect-preserving 3×3 split with white or colored borders
Adjust padding color and tile corner radius and gap if you want rounded tiles with rounded-corners preview in the feed
Download all 9 tiles as a zip file, or save individual tiles one at a time, then upload tile 1→9 to Xiaohongshu/Instagram/Moments in order
advantages: Pure Canvas client-side processing so travel shots, family photos, and commercial product imagery never leave the editing machine — no uploads, no server round-trips, no analytics on any file bytes
Three tile modes (hard crop, pad-to-square, and padded-border export) cover both the three most common social grid patterns without forcing a single manual crop workflow
Outputs ready-to-post 1080×1080 social tiles with optional rounded corners + consistent padding so tiles look intentional instead of poorly cropped when posted

faqs.q: Does this 9-grid cutter upload my photo to any server?
faqs.a: No. Every crop, resize, and tile split happens inside your browser using the HTML5 Canvas API. The original photo and all 9 generated tiles never leave your device — no network call is made and nothing is cached or stored by the tool or any third party. This makes it safe for private photos, unreleased product renders, and sensitive personal imagery.

faqs.q: What if my original photo is not a perfect 1:1 square?
faqs.a: You have three options. Hard-crop will center-crop the photo to 1:1 before splitting (great for portraits). Pad-to-square will fill extra space with a solid color of your choice without cutting content. Aspect-preserving split keeps the original ratio intact and tiles only what fits. Most Xiaohongshu and Instagram users pick pad-to-square to keep every face and subject fully visible.

faqs.q: Can I add white borders or rounded corners between tiles?
faqs.a: Yes. The cutter supports adjustable inner/outer padding in any color (white is default) and adjustable border-radius on each tile, so you can recreate the classic 宫格 (puzzle-grid) look popular on Xiaohongshu without running each tile through a separate editor.

faqs.q: Which output formats and sizes are exported?
faqs.a: Each of the 9 tiles exports as 1080×1080 PNG or JPG by default (the safe universal square post size for every major Chinese and Western social feed). The all-in-one zip bundles every numbered tiles in order so you post tile 1 first and tile 9 last — no sorting required.

faqs.q: Can I reuse the split for platforms other than Xiaohongshu and Instagram?
faqs.a: Absolutely. The numbered tiles work for any 9-image grid platform: WeChat Moments 9-grid uploads, Twitter/X multi-photo tweets, Facebook photo carousels, and Pinterest 宫格 puzzle homepages all accept the same numbered PNG/JPG set because each tile is a standard social-sized square image.

image-compressor.name: Free Online Image Compressor — JPG, PNG, WebP
image-compressor.description: Compress JPG, PNG and WebP images right in your browser. Adjustable quality, batch processing, nothing uploaded.

seo.intro: Image Compressor is a free online tool that lets you shrink JPG, PNG, and WebP photos directly in your browser. Adjust quality and size sliders per image, preview the compressed result side-by-side, and download smaller files individually or as a batch ZIP. Everything runs locally inside your browser — your images never leave your device and are never uploaded to any server, so private or sensitive photos stay fully under your control.
scenarios: Compressing product photos before uploading them to an ecommerce store or marketplace listing
Resizing holiday and travel photos to fit under email or messaging app attachment limits
Reducing screenshot and blog image sizes so web pages load faster and use less mobile bandwidth
tutorial: Click 'Upload images' or drag JPG/PNG/WebP files from your desktop onto the drop zone
Use the quality and max-dimension sliders on each image to tune compression strength
Check the side-by-side preview to confirm visual quality remains acceptable at the new file size
Download individual compressed files or click 'Download all' to save them as a ZIP bundle
advantages: Runs entirely in the browser with WebAssembly — no server round-trip, so photos stay private even when you're on public Wi-Fi
Per-image quality controls with live before/after preview let you strike an exact size-versus-quality tradeoff
Bulk export as ZIP plus batch rename makes it easy to prepare dozens of product images for a store launch in one pass

faqs.q: Are the photos I upload here ever sent to a remote server?
faqs.a: No. Image decoding, resizing, and compression all happen in your browser. Nothing leaves your device, so private photos, ID scans, and internal screenshots remain fully confidential end-to-end.

faqs.q: How do I compress an image to exactly 100KB or a specific size?
faqs.a: Switch to 'Target Size' mode, enter your desired KB (e.g., 100), and the tool will automatically find the optimal quality level through binary search. Perfect for passport photos, government forms, and social media upload limits.

faqs.q: Which output formats are available? JPG, PNG, or WebP?
faqs.a: You can choose to keep the original format or convert to JPG, PNG, or WebP. WebP typically produces the smallest file sizes while maintaining good quality, making it ideal for web publishing and social media.

faqs.q: Can I compress multiple images at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload multiple images and the tool will process them all. Each image shows its original size, compressed size, and compression percentage. You can download files individually or all at once.

faqs.q: Is there a before/after comparison feature?
faqs.a: Yes. After compression, use the slider to compare the original and compressed images side by side. This helps you verify quality before downloading and find the perfect balance between size and visual quality.

faqs.q: Should I remove EXIF metadata from my photos?
faqs.a: EXIF data contains camera settings, GPS location, and other metadata. Removing it reduces file size slightly and protects your privacy by not revealing when and where photos were taken. This is especially useful for public web uploads.

figma-json-exporter.name: Figma JSON Exporter
figma-json-exporter.description: Paste Figma page JSON to batch export PNG/SVG/PDF images. 100% in-browser processing, no file upload required.

seo.intro: Figma JSON Exporter is a free online tool that parses Figma page JSON data directly in your browser, extracts all visible layers, and exports them as PNG or SVG images. You can select all layers or specific ones, choose export format, and download individual files or as a batch ZIP. The entire process runs locally — your design data never leaves your device and is never uploaded to any server.
scenarios: Batch exporting icons and components from Figma designs for development and documentation
Exporting design artboards to create product documentation and presentations
Exporting Figma layers as SVG for website and application development
tutorial: Right-click on a page or artboard in Figma and select 'Copy'
Paste the JSON data into the tool
Select the layers you want to export (select all or individual)
Choose export format (PNG or SVG)
Click to download individual images, or 'Download all' to save as a ZIP
advantages: 100% browser-side processing, no server uploads — your design data stays secure
Supports batch export and ZIP bundling for increased productivity
PNG and SVG formats supported to meet different development needs

faqs.q: Do I need to log in to Figma?
faqs.a: No. The tool only parses the JSON data you paste — it doesn't communicate with Figma servers at all. Everything works offline in your browser.

faqs.q: What formats can I export to?
faqs.a: Currently supports PNG and SVG formats. PNG is ideal for previews and presentations, while SVG is perfect for vector graphics and development use.

faqs.q: Can I export hidden layers?
faqs.a: No. Only visible layers (visible: true) are exported. Hidden layers are automatically filtered out and won't appear in the export list.

faqs.q: Is my data uploaded to servers?
faqs.a: No. All JSON parsing, layer rendering, and file generation happens entirely in your browser. No network uploads occur at any point.

image-to-base64.name: Image to Base64
image-to-base64.description: Drag-drop local images and convert to Base64 instantly, pure frontend processing no server upload, supports JPG/PNG/WebP/SVG batch conversion.

seo.intro: Image to Base64 is a free online converter that turns local JPG, PNG, WebP, and SVG files into Base64 data URIs directly inside your browser. Drag files into the drop zone, adjust output format and max-dimension limits, then copy the resulting string or CSS url() snippet straight into an email template, CMS, or stylesheet. Every pixel stays on your device — no uploads, no server logs, and no queue wait.
scenarios: Embedding small icons and logos directly into HTML email templates so clients don't have to host or block external image files
Turning screenshots and product badges into Base64 strings for inline embedding in a single-file HTML report or knowledge base
Generating CSS background-image url() strings for inline SVGs and tiny PNG tiles without extra HTTP requests
tutorial: Drop one or more JPG/PNG/WebP/SVG files onto the upload zone or click to select them from disk
Pick the output format: raw Base64 string, HTML img tag, CSS url(), or Markdown image embed
Optional: enable resize-by-max-dimension if you want a smaller payload for email or CSS inline use
Click to copy the snippet for each file, or batch-copy all results at once for your codebase
advantages: Pure in-browser conversion with no server upload, so you can safely encode screenshots of internal dashboards, customer PII, and unreleased UI mockups
Multiple output formats (raw, HTML img, CSS url(), Markdown) let you paste the result without reformatting into whichever platform you're targeting
Batch mode with individual copy buttons lets you convert dozens of icons in one pass instead of uploading them one by one to competing tools

faqs.q: Are the images I drop here ever uploaded to a remote server or cloud bucket?
faqs.a: No. File reading, canvas encoding, and Base64 serialization all happen in-memory inside your browser using the File and Canvas APIs. Nothing is sent over the network or stored server-side, making it safe for NDAs, internal systems, and sensitive screenshots.

faqs.q: Which image formats can I convert to Base64 with this tool?
faqs.a: Most modern browsers allow JPG, PNG, WebP, SVG, and animated GIF as input. The output is always a valid data: URI with the correct MIME type, so email clients, browsers, and CMS editors can render it without extra transformation.

faqs.q: Will a very large image produce a Base64 string that breaks my email or CMS?
faqs.a: Optional resize-by-dimension and JPEG quality controls help you shrink the payload before encoding. The tool also warns when the resulting string crosses commonly cited email-safe and inline-CSS size thresholds so you can decide whether to fall back to a hosted image instead.

faqs.q: Can I convert many icons in one go instead of one file at a time?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool accepts multi-file drag-and-drop and a directory picker on supported browsers. Each converted file exposes its own copy button per output format, and you can also dump the whole batch as a JSON mapping of filename to Base64 for build pipelines.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the raw Base64 output and the 'data URI' formats?
faqs.a: Raw Base64 is just the ASCII payload; data URIs wrap it in data:;base64, which is what , CSS url(), and most email HTML editors expect. The raw form is useful when you're storing the string in a database or passing it through an API that already knows the media type.

json-formatter.name: JSON Formatter
json-formatter.description: Online JSON formatter, validator and minifier with syntax highlighting. Every developer's must-have.

seo.intro: JSON Formatter is a free online JSON formatter, validator and minifier. Paste or upload a raw JSON string, YAML snippet or GraphQL response body, and it will pretty-print with indentation, highlight syntax errors with line numbers, collapse nested objects, and optionally convert to minified one-line output with deduplicated whitespace. It supports JSON Schema draft-07 basic linting so you can spot missing fields and wrong types before pasting into an API client or config file. The whole parse-tree lives in the browser tab — your JSON payloads are never sent to a server.
scenarios: Debugging a REST or GraphQL API response that arrived minified or broken and you need readable indentation plus the exact line where parsing fails.
Formatting large JSON config files (package.json, tsconfig.json, Terraform state snippets) before committing so diffs stay clean.
Converting hand-written YAML config to clean JSON for ingestion by CLI tools or CIs that only accept strict JSON.
tutorial: Paste your raw JSON, NDJSON or YAML snippet into the left input, or drag and drop a .json/.yaml file.
Press Format to pretty-print with 2-space indent, JSONP to unwrap callback wrappers, or Validate to get errors with column and line numbers.
Use the tree view to expand or collapse nested objects and arrays, or copy the tree node you need.
Switch to Minify mode for one-line output or Download to save the result back to disk.
advantages: Shows the exact line and column where JSON.parse fails, with a red underline and a short human-readable reason.
Accepts YAML, NDJSON and JSONP inputs in one tool, no need to visit three different formatters.
Browser-only parsing: API secrets and tokens never leave your machine, even for 5 MB payloads.

faqs.q: Why does my JSON validate in Postman but fail here?
faqs.a: Most of the time it is trailing commas, single-quoted strings, comments or BOM — things JSON.parse() explicitly rejects. Our validator highlights the exact column so you can see where the spec diverges from JSON5 or loose parsers.

faqs.q: Can I format JSON lines (NDJSON / JSONL) files?
faqs.a: Yes. Paste a file with one JSON object per line and Korelyy will parse each line separately, number them, and show per-row errors if any row is malformed.

faqs.q: Does Korelyy keep my uploaded JSON configs or API tokens?
faqs.a: No. All parsing, formatting and validation takes place inside your browser tab. Neither the raw text nor the parsed tree touches any korelyy.com backend.

faqs.q: How do I convert YAML to JSON with this tool?
faqs.a: Paste YAML into the left pane, choose Auto-detect input type, then click Format. The output pane will produce strictly conforming JSON ready to save or copy.

faqs.q: Is there a way to collapse a deeply nested object so I can compare two configs?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch to Tree view and every object or array node gets a collapse toggle. You can also click a field to copy just that subtree as JSON.

keyword-spinoff-generator.name: Pun & Viral Keyword Spinoff
keyword-spinoff-generator.description: 5 industries (beauty/food/home/digital/baby) keyword banks. Input core word → pun/paradox/question/number 4 classes viral titles. 100% local, no cloud AI,...

seo.intro: Keyword Spinoff & Homophone Title Generator is a free in-browser copy-title ideation tool for short-video operators, Xiaohongshu / Douyin / Bilibili creators, e-commerce media buyers, and naming-needs users. Type one core keyword (product name, industry term, brand word, person name), pick a style (homophone pun, rhyme, idiom rework, reduplication, English homophone, number pun, dialect slang), and the tool automatically generates dozens of title variants and related keyword spinoffs, with sentiment tags, rough CTR estimates, and usage-scene suggestions — perfect for exhausting every traffic-leveraging variant of a word in one pass instead of brainstorming all day and only producing 3 ideas.
scenarios: An e-commerce media buyer runs creatives for the 'wet wipes' category. Inputs core word 'wet wipes', styles 'homophone pun + rhyme + idiom rework', produces 60 variants in one batch, filters to 12 for A/B testing, 3 of which beat the baseline CTR — saves 2 full days of title brainstorming

A Xiaohongshu beauty blogger is stuck on foundation review titles. Inputs 'foundation' + styles 'emotional resonance + counterintuitive + number homophone', generates 40 variants, picks the warning-angle variants, 4 of them break 10k views

A new D2C brand is naming a new product line. Inputs core concept word 'tea' + styles 'English homophone + reduplication + idiom rework', generates 80 variants, narrows down to 3 candidates to trademark — saves the cost of hiring a naming agency.
tutorial: Type the core keyword into the main input: a product name, industry term, person's name, or place name. 1–6 character words work best; very long sentences are not recommended.

Choose the title styles you want: homophone puns (same-sound character swaps), rhymes (same ending sound), idiom reworks (swap a character in a set idiom with your keyword), reduplication, English homophones, number puns (520/666 style), or dialect slang. Pick multiple for more comprehensive results.

Adjust filter options below: title length (short / medium / long), industry tags (beauty / mom-baby / food / digital / home goods etc.), sentiment tags (recommendation / warning / tutorial / twist / review / contrast).

Results are grouped by style in columns. Each title has a one-click copy button, a rough CTR estimate (based on historical CPT data), and platform-suitability tips. Click any title to expand 10 more variants in the same vein, or export the whole batch as Excel / CSV / Markdown / plain text for team review.
advantages: 7 stacked variant engines: same-sound/different-meaning, same-rhyme, idiom skeleton swap, English near-sound, number puns, dialect slang, and reduplicative word-formation — not just a lazy synonym replacer. One keyword genuinely produces dozens of real puns and rhymes far more than basic thesaurus tools.

Industry × sentiment tag filtering: built-in 20+ mainstream industry lexicons and 9 common copy sentiments (recommendation / warning / review / tutorial / emotional resonance / twist / suspense / exaggeration / contrast). Cross-filtered output so you never get wildly mismatched variants like baby-formula lines tagged for a skincare product.

100% browser-local, zero upload. Unreleased brand naming projects, unlaunched new-product core words, confidential creative KV keywords all safe to type in. All lexicon matching and pun generation runs entirely in the browser, no backend scraping.

faqs.q: Won't the puns be super cliché? Just the overused ones everyone has already run?
faqs.a: Not necessarily — the engine runs two filter layers: first deduplication against a global search-volume lexicon, second a recent hit-title corpus to downrank already-spammed old puns (for example tired formulas like 'XX Freedom' that have been overdone on Douyin get automatically deprioritized). Fresh new combinations are kept and ranked top, you get the lowest-spammed new variants first, not a ten-year-old joke collection.

faqs.q: Does it support English keyword homophones? Can I use it for cross-border indie site titles?
faqs.a: Yes. The English engine has four built-in variant types for English: homographs, alliteration, end-rhyme, and punchline substitution; it works for cross-border DTC site titles, Amazon 5-point bullet copy, and social media ad copy. English sentiment tags are currently fewer than Chinese ones, but core homophone and rhyme variants are fully covered.

faqs.q: Can I export to Excel for A/B testing 20 ad creatives?
faqs.a: Yes. One-click export to CSV / Excel (.xlsx) with 5 columns: Title, Style tag, Sentiment tag, rough CTR estimate, suggested platform. Paste straight into the title libraries of ad platforms like Ocean Engine / Qianchuan directly, no format conversion needed.

faqs.q: How many variants will it give me? 10 is not enough.
faqs.a: By default 20 per style. With all 7 styles enabled you get 80–140 variants in one batch, and each result row has a '10 more of the same type' button you can press repeatedly to expand infinitely. Expand to a few hundred variants is totally fine as long as your browser memory holds up.

faqs.q: Are dialect slang variants real dialect words or just made-up pronunciation puns?
faqs.a: Both. Part one: Mandarin → dialect homophone mapping (e.g. Cantonese 'mou man tai' → phonetic spelling puns); part two: dialect common-phrase skeleton swaps (Northeast 'laotie' (buddy), Sichuan 'ba shi' (great) etc.) where your core keyword is inserted into real dialect phrase skeletons — not made-up non-existent dialect words. All generated from real regional dialect corpora.

markdown-platform-adapter.name: All-Platform Markdown Adapter
markdown-platform-adapter.description: Built-in 5 platforms rules: Xiaohongshu #hashtag/WeChat head-tail blank/Bilibili blockquotes/Douyin image wrap/Zhihu; image link fix; table/code downgrade....

seo.intro: Markdown Multi-Platform Formatter is a free in-browser document format adapter for tech bloggers, WeChat Official editors, paid-knowledge authors, and indie developers. Paste your one canonical Markdown source, pick a target platform (WeChat Official, Zhihu, Juejin, Xiaohongshu, Notion, Feishu/Lark, Yuque, WordPress), and the tool automatically converts image links, code-block syntax highlighting, heading sizes, quote / list / table rendering, and each platform's specific format quirks — for example, it converts external images to base64 / image-bed uploads for WeChat Official (which blocks external image URLs), and auto-splits paragraphs with leading emoji for Xiaohongshu. Then copy with one click into the target editor: images and styles rarely need manual touch-up.
scenarios: An indie dev writes a 2000-word technical blog Markdown in VSCode, runs it through the Adapter in 'WeChat Official' mode: code highlighting becomes inline styles the WeChat editor recognizes, external images auto-convert to base64 embeds. Pasting directly into WeChat backend publishes exactly as previewed, no need to re-upload every image

A paid-course author repurposes one article for 5 platforms. With the Adapter they run the same Markdown through Zhihu / Juejin / Yuque / Feishu / Notion outputs, copy each into each platform. Heading levels, ordered-list indentation, table borders, and footnotes all adjust per platform conventions automatically, no 5x manual reformatting

A Xiaohongshu blogger runs a long Markdown post through 'Xiaohongshu' mode: auto-split into 2–3 paragraph screen chunks, inserts context-appropriate leading emoji per paragraph, adds #tags to H2s, converts code blocks to screenshot placeholders. Pasting into Xiaohongshu drafts gives a standard 5-screen readable note structure
tutorial: Paste your Markdown source into the input. GFM standard supported (fenced code, tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes), inline HTML, Mermaid diagrams, math formulas, local and remote image paths all work.

Choose a target platform: WeChat / Zhihu / Juejin / Xiaohongshu / Notion / Feishu / Yuque / WordPress. A live preview shows that platform's visual style — fonts, line height, code-block background colors all match the target editor.

Toggle per-platform options: auto-convert external images to base64, code block line numbers, add emoji / #hashtags before headings, Xiaohongshu auto-paragraph-splitting. Save different presets for different platforms.
Click 'Copy Rich Text' (for rich editors like WeChat / Zhihu / Feishu) or 'Copy Markdown' (for Markdown-native editors like Juejin / Yuque / Notion). Paste it in and the styling is already aligned.
advantages: 8 mainstream content platforms fully covered, each with a human-maintained stylesheet and format-quirk ruleset — not just one CSS file crudely reused everywhere. WeChat code inline styles, Xiaohongshu paragraph emoji, Zhihu quote formatting, Juejin heading sizes are all manually tested to match target editors.

Full image-handling pipeline: external images auto-download then embed as base64 (great for platforms that block external image URLs, like WeChat), one-click upload to your own image bed (SM.MS / Qiniu / custom POST endpoint), and images exceeding platform size limits auto-compress under the cap so pasted content never shows broken images.

Runs 100% locally in browser, zero upload. Unreleased paid-course Markdown drafts, confidential internal corporate docs, deployment tutorials with private account details all paste safely. All parsing, base64 conversion, and style assembly runs client-side with no backend scraping.

faqs.q: Will code highlighting still show after pasting into WeChat Official? Will it not just turn into black monospace plain text?
faqs.a: No — WeChat rich text editor only accepts inline style attributes, it ignores <style> tags and CSS classes. So for WeChat output the Adapter disassembles every code line's colors, font sizes, backgrounds, and highlight bars into spans with inline styles. Paste it and the highlighting is identical to the preview, no need to rework in a 3rd-party WeChat editor.

faqs.q: How are images handled? Can it auto-upload to my own image bed?
faqs.a: Three modes, you pick in options: ① Download external images and embed as base64 inline (safest, displays 100% on WeChat, but makes copied content larger); ② POST upload to a custom image-bed endpoint you fill in (SM.MS / Qiniu / self-hosted all supported, then URLs get replaced with returned links); ③ Keep original URLs untouched (good for platforms that allow hotlinking, like Zhihu / Juejin).

faqs.q: Does it support Mermaid diagrams and math formulas? Do they paste as images or as raw source?
faqs.a: Yes, by default both are supported. The Adapter renders Mermaid code blocks and $-delimited formulas into SVG / PNG screenshots locally in the browser using mermaid.js and KaTeX, then embeds per platform capability: WeChat mode converts to PNG+base64, Notion/Yuque keeps SVG, Juejin replaces with that platform's native formula syntax. You never get raw ```mermaid source stuck in your post.

faqs.q: Can it convert a 5000-word long article with 20 images in one go?
faqs.a: Absolutely. As long as images aren't multi-megabyte RAW originals, a 5000-word + 20-image Markdown parses, renders, and base64-converts locally in 5–15 seconds typically. If it hangs it's almost always an external image timing out — swap that one image for local upload in options and you're set.

faqs.q: When I copy and paste into Feishu / Notion will the formatting break?
faqs.a: No — outputs are adapted per destination. 'Copy Rich Text' mode uses clipboard HTML that Feishu, Notion, Yuque, and WordPress block editors all parse correctly into blocks. 'Copy Markdown' mode outputs each platform's native Markdown variant (Juejin code-fence aliases, Notion callout syntax, etc.) so paste produces native blocks, not a wall of plain text lines.

markdown-preview.name: Markdown Preview
markdown-preview.description: Online Markdown real-time preview editor, split pane view, support table, code highlight, task list, one-click HTML export.

seo.intro: Markdown Preview is a free online editor that renders Markdown to styled HTML in real time with a side-by-side split view. Paste your document, and tables, code blocks with syntax highlighting, task lists, headings, and admonitions all update live as you type. Everything runs locally in your browser — notes, product docs, and internal markdown stay on your device and are never sent to a server.
scenarios: Drafting a GitHub README, changelog, or developer docs and checking how the rendered HTML will look before you commit
Writing blog posts or technical articles in Markdown and previewing formatting, images, and code blocks as they'll appear on a CMS
Proofreading long-form documentation with nested tables, callouts, and checklist items without a local editor install
tutorial: Type or paste your Markdown source into the left editor pane
Use the right preview pane to review formatting, tables, code highlighting, images, and lists as they render
Toggle between split view, editor-only, and preview-only layouts depending on whether you're writing or reviewing
Copy the rendered HTML, download a standalone HTML file, or export as Markdown when you're ready to publish
advantages: Side-by-side editing with synchronized scrolling, so long documents stay in sync between the raw Markdown source and rendered preview
Supports GFM extensions including tables, fenced code with syntax highlighting, task lists, strikethrough, and autolinks exactly the way popular platforms render them
No server dependency — everything renders client-side, so private meeting notes, internal architecture docs, and unreleased release notes stay confidential

faqs.q: Which Markdown flavor does this preview support?
faqs.a: It aims at GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) parity, including standard tables, fenced code blocks, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks, and heading anchors. Common extensions like footnotes, admonitions, and definition lists are also enabled so documentation previews match most modern publishing platforms.

faqs.q: Is my document uploaded to a remote server when I paste it in?
faqs.a: No. Markdown parsing and HTML rendering happen entirely in the browser with bundled JavaScript libraries. No network call is made, no content is stored or logged, and nothing leaves your device, so private docs and unreleased launch notes are perfectly safe.

faqs.q: Can I embed images inside the Markdown preview?
faqs.a: Yes. You can reference publicly hosted images by URL, and for one-off local images you can drag files into the editor to convert them to Base64 and embed them inline so the preview renders without any internet connection.

faqs.q: How do I get the rendered HTML for my CMS or blog engine?
faqs.a: Use the 'Copy HTML' action to grab only the rendered body markup, or 'Download as HTML' to get a fully self-contained file with embedded styles that you can drop into any static site, blog theme, or email template.

faqs.q: Is there a way to check for common Markdown lint issues while I write?
faqs.a: The editor underlines broken link references, mismatched fenced code markers, and unclosed emphasis delimiters as you type, and a summary panel lists each issue with a clickable jump so you can clean up messy Markdown before exporting.

mortgage-calculator.name: Mortgage Calculator
mortgage-calculator.description: Precise monthly mortgage payment calculation. Supports equal principal-and-interest and equal-principal repayment plans with real-time breakdowns.

seo.intro: This free mortgage calculator estimates your monthly home loan payment and shows a full amortization breakdown. Enter the loan amount, annual interest rate (APR) and term in years, and it instantly returns your monthly payment, total interest paid over the life of the loan, and a schedule of how each payment splits between principal and interest. It supports both the standard equal monthly payment method (amortizing / equal principal-and-interest) and the equal-principal method where the principal portion stays fixed and payments shrink over time. Everything runs in your browser, so none of your financial figures are uploaded or stored.
scenarios: Before buying a home, check whether the monthly payment fits your budget at different loan amounts and rates.
Compare a 15-year versus a 30-year term to see how much extra total interest a longer loan costs.
Test how a larger down payment or a lower rate changes your monthly payment and lifetime interest.
tutorial: Enter the total loan amount (home price minus your down payment).
Type the annual interest rate (APR), not the monthly rate.
Choose the repayment term in years, e.g. 15, 20 or 30.
Switch between equal payment and equal-principal to compare, then read the payment and interest breakdown.
advantages: Shows a full month-by-month amortization schedule, not just a single number.
Supports both equal-payment and equal-principal repayment methods for direct comparison.
Runs entirely in your browser — your income and loan figures never leave your device.

faqs.q: What is the difference between equal payment and equal principal?
faqs.a: With equal monthly payment, you pay the same amount every month and the interest share is higher early on. With equal principal, the principal repaid each month is fixed, so early payments are larger and total interest paid is lower.

faqs.q: Should I enter a monthly or an annual interest rate?
faqs.a: Enter the annual rate (APR). The calculator divides it internally to compute the monthly interest, so you do not need to convert it yourself.

faqs.q: Can it account for early or extra repayments?
faqs.a: The base calculation assumes fixed scheduled payments. Any extra payment reduces your remaining principal, which lowers total interest — you can approximate this by lowering the loan amount or shortening the term.

faqs.q: Does the result include taxes, insurance or fees?
faqs.a: No. It calculates principal and interest only. Property tax, home insurance and loan fees vary by location and lender, so add them separately for a full monthly cost.

faqs.q: Is my financial data uploaded anywhere?
faqs.a: No. All calculations happen locally in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to a server or saved.

password-generator.name: Password Generator
password-generator.description: Create strong, random passwords with customizable length and character types. Copy with one click, all in your browser.

seo.intro: Password Generator is a free online tool that creates strong, cryptographically random passwords for accounts, Wi-Fi and encryption keys. Choose a length between 4 and 128 characters, toggle uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, symbols or the full ASCII set, and it instantly outputs one or more secure passwords you can copy to the clipboard. It also calculates estimated crack time and shows strength colour bars so you can tell at a glance whether a password is weak or strong. Everything runs locally in your browser with JavaScript crypto APIs — passwords are never transmitted or stored on any server.
scenarios: Signing up for a new email, bank or social account and you need a strong master password on the spot.
Provisioning shared Wi-Fi access codes, API keys or team vault secrets with a specific length and character mix.
Generating multiple unique passwords at once for a team onboarding batch, then copying the full list in one click.
tutorial: Open the Password Generator tool from Korelyy Tools and pick your target length with the slider.
Select which character groups to include: uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols, or enable exclude-ambiguous for handwritten use.
Click the refresh button to generate a new candidate, then review the crack-time and strength bar.
Hit the copy button to put the final password on your clipboard, or use batch mode for multiple passwords.
advantages: Uses browser Web Crypto / window.crypto for true cryptographically random output, not a weak seedable PRNG.
Shows realistic brute-force crack time and a colour-coded strength bar next to every candidate.
100% client-side with optional passphrase mode and no watermarks or uploads.

faqs.q: Are the passwords generated here really random and safe?
faqs.a: Yes. Password Generator uses window.crypto.getRandomValues, the browser-level cryptographically secure random source, not Math.random. That makes the output unpredictable and suitable for real account passwords.

faqs.q: How long should my password be for a bank or email account?
faqs.a: Aim for at least 16 characters with mixed case, numbers and one symbol. Our estimator shows the difference between a 12-char and 18-char password is several orders of magnitude in brute-force resistance.

faqs.q: Can I generate passwords that exclude tricky characters like 0 O 1 l I?
faqs.a: Yes. Turn on the Exclude Ambiguous toggle and the generator will skip zero-capital-O, one-lowercase-L and other visually confusable glyphs.

faqs.q: Does Korelyy save or log the passwords I generate?
faqs.a: Never. All computation runs inside your own browser window. Nothing is uploaded to korelyy.com, sent to analytics, or persisted beyond the current page.

faqs.q: What is the difference between random and pronounceable passphrases?
faqs.a: Random passwords are jumbles of characters, shorter but harder to memorize. Passphrases chain 4-6 dictionary words with separators — easier to type and remember, with equivalent entropy to a long random string.

pdf-merger.name: PDF Merger
pdf-merger.description: Merge multiple PDFs into a single file. Reorder, rotate, delete pages before combining. 100% browser-based, no upload needed.

seo.intro: This free online PDF merger combines multiple PDF files into a single document, right inside your browser. Add the files you want, drag them into the order you need, and download the merged PDF in one click. Because the merging happens locally on your device, your documents are never uploaded to any server — which matters when the files are invoices, contracts, or anything private. There is no watermark and no sign-up.
scenarios: Combine separate invoices, receipts or contracts into one file for accounting or archiving.
Merge multi-chapter reports, scanned pages or exported slides into a single deliverable.
Bundle a resume with a portfolio or cover letter into one PDF before sending it out.
tutorial: Add two or more PDF files from your device.
Drag the files to arrange them in the order you want them merged.
Click merge to build the combined document.
Download the resulting single PDF.
advantages: Files stay in your browser and are never uploaded, protecting private documents.
No watermark is added to the merged output.
No file-count or sign-up limits for normal use.

faqs.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. The merge runs entirely in your browser, so your PDFs never leave your device.

faqs.q: Is there a file size limit?
faqs.a: There is no hard limit, but very large files depend on your device's memory since everything is processed locally in the browser.

faqs.q: Can I change the page or file order?
faqs.a: Yes. Drag the files into the sequence you want before merging, and they will be combined in that order.

faqs.q: Will the merged PDF have a watermark?
faqs.a: No. The output is a clean merged PDF with no added watermark or branding.

faqs.q: Can I split a PDF back apart later?
faqs.a: This tool only merges. To break a PDF into pieces, use a dedicated PDF split tool.

pinyin-annotator.name: Chinese Pinyin Annotator — Add Pinyin to Text
pinyin-annotator.description: Add pinyin with tone marks to Chinese text automatically. Smart polyphonic detection, browser-local. Free for teachers, authors, and learners — no signup...

seo.intro: Pinyin Annotator is a free in-browser Hanzi pronunciation tool for Mandarin teachers, primary-school Chinese-language teachers, children's picture-book authors, self-publishers and editorial staff. Paste a Chinese article containing rare characters or polyphonic (multi-read) characters, and the tool automatically places toned pinyin above (or next to) each Hanzi. It intelligently identifies polyphonic readings (e.g. '重' as zhòng in 重要 'important' but as chóng in 重复 'repeat', choosing the most likely pronunciation via contextual word frequency), optionally skips already-annotated characters, and lets you pick annotation position (superscript above / side gloss inline / trailing parentheses). Outputs copyable rich text, PDF, Word, or pinyin-on-image — perfect for children's flashcards, CSL reading materials, or rare-character annotated classical-Chinese drafts.
scenarios: A Mandarin-as-Second-Language teacher prepares a 300-character reader for beginner class, containing 28 polyphonic characters (行 / 乐 / 中 / 了 etc.).
