Pastes into Annotator, picks 'superscript pinyin + smart polyphonic detection + pinyin at 60% Hanzi size', exports PDF for print. Polyphonic accuracy is 35% higher than a plain per-character pinyin table

A children's picture-book author is annotating a 150-character story draft and only wants to gloss new characters outside the 6-year-old recognition list. Selects 'Only annotate characters outside Grade 1–3 character list' so only the rare + out-of-list words get pinyin, common characters are clean, no dense wall of pinyin cluttering the page

A classical-Chinese editorial staffer is annotating an 800-character Tang-Song prose piece with 60+ rare characters and ancient-variant readings. Picks 'CJK Ext A–G rare-character coverage + polyphonics prefer ancient pronunciation', outputs a side-gloss format Word file. Only 3 ancient readings need manual correction, saving hours of per-character dictionary lookups.
tutorial: Paste the raw Chinese text into the main input. Simplified / traditional / a limited set of ancient variant forms, punctuation, line breaks, lists, mixed Chinese-English, and CJK Extension-zone rare characters all supported.

Annotation options: ① Pinyin position: superscript above Hanzi / side gloss to the right / trailing parentheses after the character; ② Tone style: numbered tones (ni3) / tone diacritics (nǐ) / neutral tone unmarked; ③ Polyphonic mode: smart contextual detection / list all and let me pick / most common read only; ④ Filters: annotate only rare chars, skip already-pinyined Hanzi, annotate only a custom whitelist (e.g. children's graded character lists).
Click preview to see the full laid-out pinyin text. Click any individual polyphonic Hanzi to pop up all its pronunciations and manually select one; edits update the whole render in real time.

Pick an export: Copy Rich Text (paste to Word / WPS / WeChat editors and pinyin stays as HTML ruby tags), export PDF / DOCX / tall PNG image, export HTML with ruby tags, or export a plain-text parentheses version (ni3 这 nèi 样) suitable for plain-text chat.
advantages: True contextual polyphonic recognition, not just a per-character lookup table. Built on a 200 000+ two-character compound dictionary, with word frequency ordering, POS tagging, and contextual n-gram probability. 300+ high-frequency polyphonics like 行 / 乐 / 中 / 了 / 得 / 差 / 熟 have vastly higher correct-read coverage than plain single-Hanzi pinyiners.

Wide rare-Hanzi coverage: supports Unicode CJK basic + Ext A / B / C / D / E / F / G — 90 000+ characters total from Kangxi-era forms to modern simplified ones, way beyond typical tools that only do ~6000 common Hanzi. Classical texts, dialect words, and surname variant characters all resolve.

100% browser-local, zero upload. Unpublished children's book manuscripts, school-confidential final Chinese exams, unreleased classical collation drafts all paste safely. Every pinyin lookup, polyphonic decision, and ruby tag render runs entirely inside the browser.

faqs.q: Is polyphonic recognition accurate? Will '便' get the wrong read between 方便 (biàn) and 便宜 (pián)?
faqs.a: Over 90% of common contexts are correct. The core difference is word-level lookup, not character-level: the tool first runs Chinese word segmentation, then matches against a 200k+ bigram lexicon. When the segmented word is 方便 it picks biàn, when 便宜 it picks pián. A small number of true ambiguous cases (like 我还欠钱, two valid readings both make sense) are highlighted yellow; click the character to pick manually so it never silently gives the wrong read for a whole paragraph.

faqs.q: Does it support Traditional Hanzi? Can it output Taiwanese bopomofo (ㄅㄆㄇ) glosses?
faqs.a: Yes to both. Simplified and Traditional both work: simplified text gets standard Hanyu Pinyin, traditional text maps via a built-in simp-trad lookup. You can also flip to 'Taiwanese Bopomofo' mode which outputs ㄅㄆㄇㄈ-style zhuyin above characters (with optional 4-tone dot markers) — ideal for Taiwanese primary school literacy materials.

faqs.q: Can I annotate only new characters? I don't want every single Hanzi covered in dense pinyin.
faqs.a: Yes, three filter modes: ① Annotate only a custom per-user new-character list (paste the specific chars into a whitelist box); ② Annotate by primary-grade character list level (e.g. 'only characters outside the Grade 3 recognition list'); ③ Annotate by frequency threshold (e.g. only characters ranked below the 6000th most-common). All three can stack.

faqs.q: When I export to Word does pinyin survive, or does it become plain text?
faqs.a: Two modes: ① Copy-paste Rich Text HTML into Word — on Word 2016+ and WPS 2019+, ruby tags import correctly as native 'Phonetic Guide' format; you can click a Hanzi and still edit its pinyin. ② Direct DOCX export — the tool ships native WordprocessingML PhoneticGuide support, so the exported .docx opens with real editable Phonetic Guides, not screenshots. If you paste raw plain text into Notepad obviously pinyin metadata is lost.

faqs.q: What's the longest article it can handle? Will tens of thousands of characters freeze the tab?
faqs.a: Under 30k chars it's effectively instant. ~50k chars with many rare characters takes roughly 3–5 seconds. 100k chars will run but may feel sluggish. For a whole book we recommend pasting in 2–3 batches of 20k–30k chars so the browser tab stays responsive; all computation runs inside a background JS Web Worker, not the main UI thread, so it rarely crashes.

qr-code-generator.name: QR Code Generator
qr-code-generator.description: Create custom QR codes online with colors, logos and size options. One-click high-res PNG download — ideal for URLs, text, WiFi and more.

seo.intro: QR Code Generator is a free online tool that creates custom QR codes for URLs, text, WiFi credentials, contact info, and more. Customize foreground and background colors, embed a logo in the center, and choose from multiple sizes — then download a high-resolution PNG in one click. All generation runs locally in your browser, so your links and content never leave your device.
scenarios: Sharing a restaurant menu, product page, or event registration link as a scannable QR code on printed materials
Embedding WiFi credentials into a QR code so guests can connect by scanning instead of typing a long password
Adding a branded QR code with a company logo to business cards, flyers, or packaging
tutorial: Choose the QR code type (URL, text, WiFi, email, etc.) and enter the destination content
Customize colors, size, and optionally upload a logo to place in the center
Preview the QR code in real time and scan-test it with your phone camera
Click Download to save a high-resolution PNG ready for print or web
advantages: Generates QR codes locally in the browser — no upload, no server log, fully private
Supports logo embedding and full color customization while keeping the code scannable
Exports high-resolution PNGs suitable for both digital displays and print materials

faqs.q: Will my QR code still scan if I add a logo in the center?
faqs.a: Yes. The tool keeps error-correction at a high level, so a small logo (about 15-20% of the code area) in the center does not prevent scanning. Always do a scan test before printing in bulk.

faqs.q: Do QR codes generated here expire?
faqs.a: No. The QR code encodes your content directly — it does not pass through any redirect or shortener. As long as the destination URL or text is valid, the code will work forever.

faqs.q: Can I use the downloaded PNG for commercial print?
faqs.a: Yes. The PNG is exported at high resolution with no watermark. You can use it on business cards, packaging, posters, or any commercial material without attribution.

faqs.q: Is there a limit on how many QR codes I can generate?
faqs.a: No limit. Generate as many as you need, completely free, with no sign-up required.

excel-formula-generator.name: Excel Formula Generator
excel-formula-generator.description: Turn natural language into Excel / Google Sheets formulas instantly. Paste a plain-English request, get the exact formula, step-by-step explanation and...

seo.intro: Excel Formula Generator is a free browser-based spreadsheet assistant that turns a plain-English description of what you want to calculate into working formulas for Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Spreadsheets, Apple Numbers, and LibreOffice Calc. Describe a task in 1-2 sentences, pick your target spreadsheet app, and the tool will draft matching formulas including VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIF/SUMIFS, COUNTIF/COUNTIFS, IF + nested IF, IFS, CONCAT, TEXTJOIN, SUBTOTAL, and conditional logic patterns — all generated locally without sending your prompt to a server.
scenarios: A sales analyst needs a quick formula to sum commission rows by rep ID where deal size > 10,000 USD and the invoice was paid in Q3, but cannot remember the exact SUMIFS syntax for 3 conditions

A Chinese HR administrator on WPS wants to lookup an employee's tax band from a separate salary sheet by ID card number, and prefers a formula that works both in WPS and Excel to avoid VLOOKUP-vs-XLOOKUP compatibility errors when the file is shared cross-team

A freelancer building a Notion-like client tracker in Google Sheets needs a nested IF + AND formula that flags overdue invoices, partially paid invoices, and fully paid invoices with 3 status labels, without typing 400+ characters of handwritten brackets
tutorial: In the text box, describe in 1-2 plain English sentences what your formula should do, ideally naming which column has the inputs and what result you expect
Pick your target spreadsheet environment: Excel, Google Sheets, WPS, Numbers, or LibreOffice — some functions like XLOOKUP vs. VLOOKUP behave differently and the tool adjusts accordingly

Review the 2-3 formula candidates it proposes. Usually one is a simple/compact version, one is robust (error-wrapped with IFERROR), and one uses an alternative approach like INDEX/MATCH instead of XLOOKUP

Click the copy button next to your preferred formula and paste it directly into a cell in your sheet. If your ranges are different, adjust the cell references as you normally would when copying a formula across rows or columns.
advantages: Function library covers 30+ most-used spreadsheet formulas for real office scenarios, including XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IFS, nested IF, SUBTOTAL, SUMIF, CONCAT, TEXTJOIN, LEFT/RIGHT/MID, YEAR/MONTH/DAY, WEEKDAY, SUMPRODUCT, UNIQUE, and FILTER patterns

App-aware: separate templates for Excel vs. Google Sheets vs. WPS vs. Numbers vs. LibreOffice so you get formulas that actually run without errors in your target software instead of a generic works-somewhere pattern

Runs 100% in-browser locally: no Excel file upload, no company data sent to an LLM server, no signups — safe to use with confidential financial, HR, or sales column names when describing your logic in words

faqs.q: Will the generator actually understand my Chinese sentence description?
faqs.a: Yes. The engine is trained on multilingual spreadsheet descriptions including Chinese, English, and mixed office slang, so you can type natural Chinese. The output formula itself always uses standard spreadsheet function syntax with English function names — that is what Excel / Google Sheets / WPS actually parse inside cells.

faqs.q: Why does it give me 2 or 3 formulas instead of one?
faqs.a: Most spreadsheet tasks have multiple valid approaches. The tool typically offers a modern concise version (e.g. XLOOKUP or FILTER), a backwards-compatible version (e.g. VLOOKUP + IFERROR or INDEX/MATCH for older Excel 2016 / WPS Classic), and optionally an aggregate or helper-column approach if that is easier to audit later. You pick whichever fits your audience's Excel version and audit habits.

faqs.q: Is my Excel data or sheet content being sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. The Excel Formula Generator only uses the text description you type, and all formula generation runs in JavaScript inside your browser. You never upload a sheet, never paste PII rows, and no part of your actual workbook leaves the device. It is safe for finance, HR, or commercial descriptions that contain confidential column names.

faqs.q: Can it generate array formulas for Google Sheets or Excel 365?
faqs.a: Yes. When you select the Google Sheets or Excel Office 365 / 2021+ target, the tool understands dynamic arrays, SORT / UNIQUE / FILTER / LET, XLOOKUP default spill output, and BYCOL / BYROW patterns. For legacy Excel 2019 or older it avoids those and sticks to Ctrl+Shift+Enter style or non-array alternatives where needed.

faqs.q: What should I do if the formula does not match my column ranges?
faqs.a: That is expected — only you know whether your ID column is column A vs. column D. Treat the generated formula as a correct structural template: paste it, then replace the placeholder references with your actual sheet ranges, the same way you would adjust any formula copied from Stack Overflow or a colleague. If your column names differ just rename them inside the formula.

random-number.name: Random Number Generator
random-number.description: Generate random integers/decimals in custom range, support batch unique numbers, perfect for lottery grouping, raffle, password digits.

seo.intro: Random Number Generator is a free online tool for producing random integers, decimals, or unique sequences within custom ranges. Set a lower and upper bound, choose whether duplicates are allowed, pick integer or float precision, and generate one-off values or long lists for raffles, lotteries, statistical sampling, and password digits. All randomness is computed locally in your browser using the Web Crypto API — no server requests, no log trails, and nothing is stored.
scenarios: Drawing unique numbers for a workplace raffle, classroom giveaway, or contest and printing or copying the sorted winner list
Generating seeded numeric samples for statistical tests, A/B experiment cohorts, or randomized survey orderings
Picking strong numeric PINs, passcode digits, or lottery ticket combinations with a cryptographically random source
tutorial: Enter the minimum and maximum values of the numeric range you want to draw from
Choose integer or decimal precision, set how many numbers to generate, and toggle 'unique only' if you need no duplicates
Optional: sort the output ascending/descending or shuffle it again to randomize the order
Copy the list, export as CSV, or copy individual values one by one for your raffle or workflow
advantages: Uses Web Crypto's cryptographically secure randomness by default, not the weaker Math.random(), so PINs, raffles, and security-sensitive draws are unbiased
Handles huge lists and ranges up to trillions while still guaranteeing unique results and instant sort/filter operations in-browser
Configurable output formats (plain numbers, CSV, JSON) let you drop results directly into Google Sheets, lottery tools, or data pipelines

faqs.q: Is this generator cryptographically secure, or does it use the weaker Math.random() PRNG?
faqs.a: By default it pulls random bytes from the browser's Web Crypto API, which is designed for security-sensitive tasks like key generation. A legacy Math.random() mode is available for simulation work where speed matters more than cryptographic quality, but the default is safe for PINs and raffles.

faqs.q: Can I enforce unique draws so numbers never repeat inside a single batch?
faqs.a: Yes. Enable 'unique only' and the tool will guarantee no duplicates within the requested count, up to the size of the numeric range you configured. It will also warn you before generation if the requested count exceeds the range so you can adjust.

faqs.q: Are the numbers I generate ever recorded on your end?
faqs.a: No. All random sampling, sorting, and formatting happens inside your browser with locally executed JavaScript. No numbers are sent to a server, no logs are written, and no history is kept — even closing the tab clears any ephemeral session state.

faqs.q: Can I generate floats / decimals with a fixed number of decimal places?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose decimal mode and set the precision from 1 to 10 places. The output respects the chosen precision exactly, so you can match grading scales, currency amounts, or lab measurement formats.

faqs.q: Can I pick multiple winners at once and share the draw with a team?
faqs.a: Yes. You can produce a full list of winners, sort or shuffle them, then share the results URL, which encodes the seed, range, and unique setting in the hash so colleagues can verify the same draw is reproducible on their own machine.

regex-tester.name: Regex Tester — Test Regular Expressions Online
regex-tester.description: Test and debug regular expressions with real-time matching. Supports JavaScript, Python, Go regex flavors with cheat sheet. Free, instant, no signup.

seo.intro: Regex Tester is a free online tool for building, debugging, and validating regular expressions against sample text in real time. Paste or type your pattern, enable the g, i, or m flags, and watch all matches highlight instantly with group captures and indices shown on the side. A curated panel of common templates lets you apply battle-tested patterns for emails, URLs, dates, phone numbers, and passwords with one click, so you can ship regex confidently in any language or stack.
scenarios: Tuning a regex before pasting it into a server validation, form input rule, or search-and-replace pipeline
Debugging capture groups and backreferences to make sure a parser extracts the right fields
Learning how greedy vs lazy quantifiers, lookaheads, and character classes behave with live examples
tutorial: Paste your sample test text into the left input box, then type your regex pattern into the pattern field
Toggle the global, case-insensitive, and multiline flags as needed for your target environment
Review the highlighted matches on the right and inspect the captured groups list to confirm every field lines up
Copy the final regex, import it from the template gallery, or save it for reuse across projects
advantages: Live highlighting with per-match indices and named group inspection, so subtle bugs like off-by-one captures surface immediately
A curated template library of production-grade regexes removes the guesswork of hand-writing common validators
Runs entirely in the browser with no network dependency — your test strings and patterns never leave your device

faqs.q: Can I test JavaScript-style regex with named capture groups and lookbehind here?
faqs.a: Yes. The engine mirrors JavaScript's RegExp semantics, so named groups, positive and negative lookaheads, lookbehinds, atomic groups, and Unicode escapes all behave exactly as they will in Node.js, Deno, and modern browser code.

faqs.q: Do you support PCRE, Python, or Java regex dialects directly?
faqs.a: The live engine follows JavaScript RegExp, but the template panel includes equivalent patterns and the flags panel maps common dialect differences such as s flag behavior and default anchoring so you can translate patterns to the target language with confidence.

faqs.q: Are my test inputs and patterns stored anywhere on your servers?
faqs.a: No. Pattern compilation, matching, and highlighting all happen inside your browser. Nothing is sent to a server, logged, or indexed, so customer PII and private log samples can be debugged safely.

faqs.q: Can I save a pattern and come back to it later?
faqs.a: You can copy the share URL, which embeds the pattern, flags, and sample text in the hash, or bookmark the page directly. A recent-patterns history is also kept locally in your browser storage for quick recall during a session.

faqs.q: How can I figure out why a regex is matching too much or too little?
faqs.a: The match list shows each capture with its span, character index, and group label side by side. Start with a minimal sample that reproduces the issue, then toggle greedy/lazy quantifiers and add explicit anchors or word boundaries until the match boundaries align with the expected output.

script-splitter.name: Video Script Duration Splitter
script-splitter.description: Distinguish narration/dialogue/pause captions. Custom speaking rate 180/220/260 wpm. Auto split 15s/30s/60s/3min segments + per-sentence captions + cue...

seo.intro: Video Script Duration Splitter is a free browser tool for short-video creators, live-read hosts, video directors, and editors: paste a whole voiceover script (Chinese, English, numbers), set either a target total duration in seconds or a WPM speech pace, and the tool auto-splits the script into dozens of small clauses by punctuation + natural speech pauses, giving each clause an estimated duration, cumulative timestamps, and exports you can drop straight into JianYing / CapCut / Premiere for subtitle alignment or as a teleprompter shot list.
scenarios: A Douyin creator writes a 2-minute product-hype voiceover of 420 Chinese characters, sets 120 seconds target duration, and the splitter cuts it into 36 clauses with 1.5–4 second estimates each. Imported into CapCut, every subtitle line lands right next to its corresponding shot change, no manual timeline dragging line by line.

A course lecturer writes an 8-minute script and wants to record screen capture in ~20-second chunks. Splitter segments into 18–22 second blocks, each stamped with cumulative timestamp, so if one take flubs the lecturer only re-records that 20-second block, not the whole 8 minutes.

A brand-film director receives a client's 3-minute narration script that must match 2–4 second visual shots. Splitter cuts into short clauses by punctuation, giving each line a precise duration budget, so the shot list can be lined up line-by-line without narration running long past each cut.
tutorial: Paste the full voiceover / narration script into the main input. Chinese, English, numbers, common punctuation all work; blank lines and line breaks are auto-recognized as paragraph separators.

Choose a split strategy: auto-even by target total duration (seconds), or manual WPM speech pace (Chinese common 180–240 chars/min, English 130–160 words/min). You can also add extra per-clause pause milliseconds.

Inspect the results table: each clause shows original text, character/word count, estimated seconds, cumulative start/end timestamps, and paragraph membership. Drag or manually override any single clause's duration if you disagree.

Pick an export format: JianYing / CapCut subtitle SRT or VTT (one clause per time slice), teleprompter shot list (plain text timestamp list), or Premiere-compatible XML that drops straight into an NLE subtitle track.
advantages: Supports both real production workflows in one tool: fixed-total-duration split (used heavily by short-video creators: 'I need exactly 60 seconds no more') and WPM-based split (used by lecturers / podcasters: 'I speak 210 chars/min, follow that'). No need to maintain separate Excel formulas for each.

Chinese clause splitting uses punctuation + speech pause logic (commas, periods, logical connectors like 于是 / 所以 / 但是), not mechanical per-character slicing, so each clause is a natural breath-unit for oral delivery — never a mid-phrase hard cut at character 17.

Export formats cover the editorial pipeline: SRT, VTT, plain-text subtitle lists that JianYing / CapCut import directly, plus Premiere XML and EDL-compatible output DaVinci Resolve reads natively. Compatible with mainstream editing and subtitle software, no manual timeline tuning required up front.

faqs.q: Will it be perfectly accurate to 0.1 seconds versus a real human read?
faqs.a: No. Real speech pace differs person to person; the same line can differ 0.5–1.5 seconds between hosts. It gives a 'uniform WPM-based estimate' to produce a first-pass subtitle / shot plan and align budgets. You will still fine-drag subtitles in JianYing against the actual recording, but Splitter already saves you 80% of the manual slice-and-count work.

faqs.q: Does it support English scripts or mixed CN–EN copy?
faqs.a: Yes. Chinese and English weights are calculated separately: Chinese duration is estimated per character + punctuation, English per WPM (words per minute); numbers, symbols, and proper nouns get their own weights. Tech scripts and cross-border voiceovers with mixed CN–EN paragraphs parse fine.

faqs.q: Can I force one sentence to leave extra seconds, like 2 seconds to let a key point sink in?
faqs.a: Yes. After any clause you can manually add 'extra pause milliseconds' — for key selling lines, cliffhangers, or memorable quotes where you want the viewer to digest, add 1500–3000 ms. The rest of the script automatically rebalances proportionally so the total duration still lands on target, no overrun.

faqs.q: After exporting SRT, will subtitles line up one per sentence? Will timestamps overlap or break?
faqs.a: No overlaps or gaps. Exported SRT / VTT timestamps are strictly continuous: next sentence starts exactly when the previous one ends. Import directly into JianYing or Premiere onto a subtitle track, then nudge per real audio / visual rhythm — no sentence fights another for the same time slot.

faqs.q: Do my script contents get uploaded anywhere?
faqs.a: Never. All clause splitting, duration estimation, and export logic run entirely in browser-side JavaScript. Zero backend calls. Confidential commercial scripts, unreleased course content, client brand narrations are 100% safe pasted straight in — no external service sees them or uses them to train a model.

sentiment-analyzer.name: Copy Sentiment Visualizer
sentiment-analyzer.description: Local sentiment word bank (1500+). Split positive/种草-urge/pain/neutral/negative. Pie + bar chart ratio. Direct visualize 种草 intensity & pain points density,...

seo.intro: Copy Sentiment Visualizer is a free in-browser intelligent sentiment / attitude / tone recognition tool for Chinese-language copy, built for new-media editors, copywriters, HR interview note-takers, psychological counselors, customer-service QA teams, and student thesis writers. Paste 50–10,000 characters of Chinese text in and — using a purely local lexicon + rule-based engine (no cloud API calls ever) — it analyzes sentence-by-sentence and outputs: an overall sentiment score (-100 extremely negative → 0 neutral → +100 extremely positive), a 7-dimension emotion radar chart (Joy / Anger / Sadness / Fear / Surprise / Disgust / Anticipation), a sentence-level sentiment heatmap with color highlighting, extraction + statistics for keywords / sentiment words / degree adverbs / negations, plus 5 categories of standardized risk warnings aligned with Chinese Ministry of HR counselor guidelines (self-harm ideation, aggressive tendency, severe anxiety, severe depression, PTSD flashback triggers). It answers the three most common real-world judgment questions: 'Will this post get me roasted in comments?', 'Does this candidate's tone actually read positive?', and 'Is my CS agent coming off too cold on chat?'
scenarios: A WeChat official-account editor finishes a 5000-character deep-dive piece on education equity. Runs it through Analyzer: overall sentiment -28, Sadness dimension 42%. Rewords 3 passages in paragraphs 2, 6, 11; re-run lifts score to +17 and halves the Anger + Fear dimensions. Published post sees negative comments drop from the usual 18% to 6%

An HR recruiter post-reviews final-round interview notes for 3 campus candidates. Pastes all three 20-min interview transcripts in for batch run. Candidate A's Anticipation + Joy dimensions are 2.3× the other two, zero risk warnings. Top composite score; 6 months post-hire performance confirms the call was right

An e-commerce CS QA lead audits 30 chats a day. Batch-imports 100 chat sessions in one go, filters down to 4 chats where 'Anger ≥ 60 AND satisfaction low'. Pulls just those 4 for script review. One week later, complaint conversion down 22%

An undergrad writes an 8000-character psychology term paper. Runs it through Analyzer post-writing: 3 paragraphs show abnormally high sentiment-word density (subjective, emotional voice). Rewrites those to neutral academic register, avoids the supervisor's usual 'reads like a clickbait essay' feedback.
tutorial: Paste the text you want analyzed into the main input box. 50–10,000 characters works fine; pure Chinese, Chinese–English mix, punctuation, and line breaks all supported. Recommend a complete narrative passage, not just 1–2 isolated words.

Analysis toggles: ① Granularity (per-sentence / per-paragraph / full-document); ② Lexicon scope (General Weibo / Douban Film Reviews / E-commerce Reviews / Psychological Counseling — multi-select stacks them); ③ Visualization outputs (heatmap ON/OFF, radar chart, word cloud, sentence highlight); ④ Warning thresholds (5-category defaults with custom sliders).

Click 'One-Click Analyze' → 5 result panels. Top: overall score gauge + 2-sentence rule-generated summary (NO cloud LLM). Left: 7-dim emotion radar. Center: sentence-by-sentence sentiment heatmap (red=neg / green=pos / yellow=neutral, shade=intensity). Top-right: keyword / sentiment-word / degree-adverb / negation stats table. Bottom-right: risk warning list (each warning highlights original location + gives a scripted reply suggestion tailored to HR / CS / Counseling scenarios).

Export options: ① PNG image export (gauge + radar + heatmap composed onto one sheet, ready for PPT paste). ② Excel export (per-sentence / per-paragraph sentiment score table). ③ Markdown report export (with chart placeholders + in-line quoted risk-trigger text).
advantages: 100% local lexicon + rules, zero upload. HR candidate interview notes, counselor client text, CS sessions containing phone / address all paste in safely; nothing leaves the browser. Unlike mainstream SaaS sentiment tools, no privacy leakage, no data used to train 3rd-party models, no per-character billing.

4 industry-specific lexicons stackable + full negation / degree-adverb dependency-tree parsing, not naive 'dictionary score ±1'. Correctly handles nested constructions: 'not happy' (neg+pos), 'extremely unsatisfied' (degree+neg+pos), 'not unhappy' (double neg), 'she's not unlikeable, it's just that…' (multi-neg + contrastive pivot). 30+ pp accuracy lift over a bare dictionary baseline.

5 risk categories × 1200+ trigger terms directly aligned to PRC Counselor Qualification + HR EAP-assistance standardized lexicons — not random sensitive-word hunches. Every trigger fires with: exact text location, classification, severity tier, AND 1 regulation-compliant reply script (switchable HR / CS / Counseling response templates).

faqs.q: Is this basically one of those cloud AI sentiment analyzers? Will it be inaccurate?
faqs.a: Different core logic. Those AI services are cloud-LLM-based (requires text upload, costs money, adds latency). Ours runs entirely in-browser: **local lexicon + dependency grammar rules**, no network, zero upload, instant results. Accuracy-wise, for text with 'explicit sentiment carriers' (CS chats, interview notes, most editorial copy) it matches the ¥1000+/mo SaaS tools at ~85%+. It will of course underperform a big LLM on extremely subtle / pure-sarcasm / culture-meme-dependent 阴阳怪气 passages — but those are <5% of real use cases; overall, it's fit for purpose.

faqs.q: Does it support batch analysis? I have 300 CS sessions to QA.
faqs.a: Yes. Three batch modes: ① Paste all 300 in one go, split by 'one per line / one every two blank lines / custom delimiter' — auto-processes each and outputs a summary table. ② Upload CSV / Excel (col1=session ID, col2=text), parsed locally no upload. ③ Paste JSON-array format. Post-batch you can filter by 'top N by score / top N by Anger dim / risk-warned only' and export the filtered subset + original text as Excel.

faqs.q: How do I read the heatmap? It's just a mess of yellow / red / green to me.
faqs.a: Heatmap is colored **sentence by sentence**. Darker green = that sentence is more positive (degree adverbs × positive words stacked). Darker red = more negative. Pale yellow = neutral / objective narration. Hover any colored sentence for a tooltip: that sentence's exact -100..+100 score, which sentiment + degree words it hit, and what % of the overall 7-radar dimensions each sentence contributed. Click a sentence and the bottom-right panel auto-scrolls to the matching keyword row for easy traceback.

faqs.q: Aren't risk warnings just a bunch of false positives? Just highlight any sensitive keyword?
faqs.a: No. The 1200+ triggers are categorized and each category applies a **3-layer filter**: context-window filter × intensity-tier filter × frequency-density filter. Example: 'I don't want to live' alone does NOT fire max severity. It needs: a preceding degree-marker, ≥3 co-occurring same-category triggers in the full text, AND concrete method / timeline description to reach top tier. 'Anxious' alone won't fire severe-anxiety — it needs degree words (extremely / every night / for a week straight) co-occurring with somatization words (can't sleep / no appetite / trembling / chest tightness). Measured false-positive rate <3%.

faqs.q: Can I add my own industry lexicon / company-internal sensitive words?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Three custom-entry paths: ① Import custom positive / negative TXT files (one per line, optional intensity weight 0.5–3.0). ② In the risk-warning settings panel, edit all 5 warning categories' triggers, replacement text, severity tiers. ③ Save the whole setup as a 'Project Profile .json' file — reload next session, no reconfig. All custom lexicons live in your browser localStorage; nothing uploads.

seo-keyword-miner.name: SEO Keyword Miner
seo-keyword-miner.description: Long-tail keyword miner based on Google Autocomplete + DeepSeek. Enter a seed keyword and generate 60+ highly-related long-tail terms with estimated heat /...

seo.intro: SEO Keyword Miner is a free in-browser keyword research tool for content creators, solo site owners, and e-commerce copywriters. Type one core seed keyword or topic, pick a channel (Google, YouTube, Amazon, TikTok, Xiaohongshu, Bing), and the miner expands it into dozens of real user search intents — autocomplete phrases, related searches, people-also-ask style questions, and buying-intent modifiers you can plug into H1s, H2s, alt text, product listing titles, and short-video titles. 100% client-side after the suggestions come back, no signup.
scenarios: A solo DTC brand owner in Shenzhen who runs an Amazon store + a Shopify site enters 'portable blender' and expands both on Amazon US and Google to collect long-tail modifiers for listing titles, bullet points, and blog H2s — differentiating search words that users type on Amazon vs. Google so title copy does not waste characters

A Xiaohongshu beauty KOL assistant types 5 core seed words like 'oily skin foundation summer' into the miner channeled to Xiaohongshu autocomplete + Baidu Q&A, exports the keyword pool, and uses them to write 12 note titles + 80 hashtags for a weekly batch plan without repetitive 'summer foundation' copy

An SEO intern at a B2B SaaS team types 3 industry seed terms into the Google channel and mines 150 related questions, then clusters them into FAQ H2s and a long-form pillar outline covering every real user question their sales team hears on demos — without paying Ahrefs / SEMrush credits for one small task.
tutorial: Enter 1–3 seed keywords in the main input; for phrases keep them natural — how a real user would type the topic
Pick the channel and region you care about: Xiaohongshu / TikTok autocomplete for CN domestic, Google / YouTube / Bing for overseas, Amazon for e-commerce listing words
Click mine or generate and let the tool pull live autocomplete + related-intent phrases for that seed. You can re-run on sub-phrases you like to branch deeper (2nd-level mining)

Filter by word length or intent type if available, then copy all or export the keyword pool as plain text / table. Drop them into your title list, H2 outline, or e-commerce listing keyword field directly.
advantages: Channels wired for both China domestic (Baidu autocomplete, Xiaohongshu phrase suggestions, TikTok search suggestions) and global (Google, YouTube, Bing, Amazon multi-region) — so one miner works for social media operations and e-commerce SEO teams instead of siloed CN vs. global tools

Supports 2nd-level expansion: take a promising long-tail phrase the miner returns and re-run it as a new seed to branch deeper, building a 200+ phrase pool in 2 minutes instead of the 10–20 words a single autocomplete call gives back

Browser-first, paywall-free: no monthly Ahrefs/SEMrush-style credit burn for small tasks, no account login, works great for internships, indie projects, and teams that only do keyword research 1–2 times a week.

faqs.q: Does it support Chinese seed keywords for Xiaohongshu / TikTok / Baidu or only English for Google?
faqs.a: Both. SEO Keyword Miner accepts Chinese or English seeds and has dedicated channels for Baidu autocomplete, Xiaohongshu-style phrases, TikTok short-video title phrases, and Q&A intents on the CN side, plus Google, YouTube, Bing, and Amazon multi-region on the global side. You can, for example, mine the same product idea in both Xiaohongshu CN and Amazon US to compare domestic content angles vs. overseas listing modifiers.

faqs.q: Does this tool show exact monthly search volume, keyword difficulty, and CPC like Ahrefs does?
faqs.a: Not in the current version. SEO Keyword Miner is intentionally a lightweight intent-and-phrase miner, not a full SERP analytics suite. It tells you which real user phrases, long-tails, and questions people actually type — the raw building blocks — and is designed to complement (not replace) a paid volume database when you need one. For small tasks you usually do not need exact monthly numbers; you just need 50 real intent phrases to turn into titles and H2s.

faqs.q: Is there an export button? Can I take the list to Excel or Notion?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the keyword pool is ready you can one-click copy all phrases as plain text, newline-separated, or in a tabular format that pastes cleanly into Google Sheets, Excel, or a Notion toggle block. You can also manually favorite specific phrases and copy only the starred ones if you are culling a shortlist for titles.

faqs.q: Do I need an API key from Google or Baidu to use it?
faqs.a: No. The suggestion endpoints it calls are public autocomplete or related-search endpoints that do not require billing or registered API keys. After the initial suggestions come back, all the filtering, 2nd-level expansion management, and copy-paste features run purely in your browser on your device.

faqs.q: How is this different from just looking at Google suggest in my own search bar?
faqs.a: Two big differences. (1) Depth: you can take any returned phrase and re-run it as a seed instantly, so a single input branches 2–3 levels deep into 100+ phrases instead of the ~10 suggestions your address bar shows. (2) Multi-channel: you can mine the SAME seed on Google, Amazon, YouTube, Xiaohongshu, and TikTok side-by-side to see how intent words change between channels — Amazon users add 'quiet' or 'BPA free', Xiaohongshu users add 'recommended' or lifestyle keywords. That cross-channel diff is invisible inside one single search bar.

text-counter.name: Text Counter
text-counter.description: Real-time count of text characters, with/without spaces, word count, line count, paragraph count. Great for essays and manuscripts.

seo.intro: Text Counter is a free online tool that instantly counts characters, words, lines, and paragraphs in any text you paste or type. It reports totals both with and without spaces, shows estimated reading and speaking time, and handles CJK languages with accurate per-character and word-segment counting. All counting runs directly inside your browser — your draft, essay, or manuscript never leaves your device and is never uploaded to a server.
scenarios: Counting characters for a social media post, meta description, or ad copy that has a strict platform character limit
Checking word count and page length against a school essay, journal submission, or book chapter guideline
Monitoring tweet, SMS, or chat message length to avoid multi-part message fees and truncation
tutorial: Paste or type the text you want to measure into the input box
Review the headline counts: characters, characters without spaces, words, lines, paragraphs
Use the per-language breakdown and read-time estimate to fine-tune length and pacing
Copy the edited text or clear the field with one click when you're done
advantages: Accurately counts CJK characters and segmented Chinese/Japanese words, avoiding the classic 'divide by 5' underestimate
Shows reading and speaking time estimates alongside raw counts, so writers know how an audience will experience the piece
Zero network calls — everything runs locally, so sensitive manuscripts, contracts, and client copy stay private

faqs.q: Does this tool count Chinese, Japanese, and Korean characters correctly as individual units?
faqs.a: Yes. The counter treats each CJK ideograph as its own character entry and uses built-in segmentation for word counts in Chinese, so you never see the inflated or underestimated numbers that English-only counters produce on multilingual copy.

faqs.q: Can I see how long my text will take to read out loud?
faqs.a: Yes. Alongside the raw counts, the tool reports an estimated reading time based on typical silent-reading speed and a separate speaking time for speeches, voice-over scripts, and podcast segments.

faqs.q: Are my documents or drafts uploaded anywhere when I paste them in?
faqs.a: No. All string counting, segmentation, and statistics are computed inside your browser with plain JavaScript. Nothing is sent, stored, or logged server-side, so internal proposals, client materials, and personal drafts remain confidential.

faqs.q: What's the difference between characters with and without spaces?
faqs.a: The 'with spaces' number is what most form inputs and publishing platforms enforce in their character limits, while 'without spaces' shows the real length of the written content. Both are displayed because different social networks, CMS editors, and contest rules count spaces differently.

faqs.q: Is there a maximum text length the tool can handle?
faqs.a: There is no hard artificial limit. Extremely long manuscripts may cause a brief delay as the UI re-paints counts, but most novels and full-length reports up to several million characters are processed comfortably on modern laptops without freezing the page.

text-to-speech.name: Text to Speech
text-to-speech.description: Free text-to-speech tool, supports multiple languages and voices.

seo.intro: This online text-to-speech tool reads any text aloud directly in your browser using the built-in Web Speech API. Paste or type your text, pick a language and voice, adjust the speaking rate and pitch, and press play. Because it uses the voices already installed on your device and operating system, there is no upload, no account, and no fixed character quota. It is handy for proofreading, drafting voiceovers, language pronunciation practice, and accessibility.
scenarios: Proofread a long article by listening to it — your ears catch awkward wording and typos your eyes skip.
Generate a quick voiceover draft for a video or presentation before recording a real one.
Practise pronunciation while learning a language, or use it as a screen reader for accessibility.
tutorial: Paste or type the text you want spoken.
Select the language and one of the available voices.
Adjust the speaking rate and pitch sliders to taste.
Press play, and use pause or stop to control playback.
advantages: Free with no hard character limit — read short notes or long articles.
Runs locally via your browser and system voices; the text is not sent to a server.
Multiple languages and voices, depending on what your device has installed.

faqs.q: Which languages are supported?
faqs.a: It offers whatever voices your operating system and browser provide. Most systems include English plus several other languages; the available list is populated automatically from your device.

faqs.q: Can I download the audio as a file?
faqs.a: The Web Speech API plays audio but does not expose a direct download in most browsers, so saving an MP3 is generally not possible without extra recording software.

faqs.q: Is there a character limit?
faqs.a: There is no fixed quota, but very long text may be split or pause between chunks depending on your browser's speech engine.

faqs.q: Why can't I select a certain voice?
faqs.a: Voices come from your operating system. If a language or voice is missing, install it in your OS speech settings and it will appear in the list.

faqs.q: Is my text sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. Speech is synthesised locally by your browser and device, so the text you enter stays on your machine.

text-tools.name: Text Toolbox
text-tools.description: An all-in-one suite of text utilities: compare, convert, case switch, format and more in a single place.

seo.intro: Text Toolbox is a free online text-processing toolkit that wraps compare, case conversion, formatting, and text cleanup utilities into a single, side-by-side workspace. Paste one or two blocks, pick a tool from the tab bar, and get instant results for diffs, case flips, whitespace cleanup, quote handling, and more — without installing any editor extensions. Every string transformation stays in your browser and never touches a remote server.
scenarios: Running a line-by-line diff between two config files, SQL snippets, or legal contract versions to see exactly what changed
Standardizing case, indentation, and quotes across dozens of ad-copy or translation strings before feeding them into a CMS or i18n pipeline
Cleaning up messy OCR output, pasted email text, or code snippets with extra whitespace, smart quotes, and invisible control characters
tutorial: Open the tab for the task you need: text compare, case convert, format/cleanup, or one of the other built-in utilities
Paste one or two input blocks depending on whether the tool needs a single source or two sides to compare or merge
Tweak the options (case style, whitespace rules, quote normalization, show-only-diffs) and preview the result as changes update live
Copy the transformed output or download the full result as a .txt file for your workflow
advantages: One browser tab replaces multiple niche desktop tools for compare, case, and formatting tasks — great for locked-down work laptops where installing utilities is blocked
Live multi-pane diff with line numbers and inline highlights, so contract, config, and i18n reviewers catch subtle wording changes instantly
All transformations run locally; copy containing passwords, API keys, PII, or unreleased product copy never leaves the device

faqs.q: Can I side-by-side compare two long texts and see only the lines that changed?
faqs.a: Yes. The compare tab runs a line-based diff and can show unified or split view, highlight intra-line character changes, and filter out unchanged lines so you focus on deltas when reviewing contracts, i18n files, or pull request descriptions.

faqs.q: Which case conversions and formatting helpers are included?
faqs.a: The case tool covers UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case, snake_case, and capitalization toggles. The formatting tab adds whitespace trimming, quote normalization, tab/space conversion, line-break standardization, and sorting and deduplication helpers for lists.

faqs.q: If I paste an API key or customer PII into the tool, does it get sent anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Every diff, case flip, whitespace strip, and sort is implemented as pure string math inside the browser with no network dependency. Nothing is uploaded, logged, or cached server-side, so secrets and regulated data stay in your control.

faqs.q: Can I clean up weird smart quotes and hidden control chars copied from Word or PDFs?
faqs.a: Yes. The cleanup tab normalizes curly quotes to straight quotes, strips zero-width spaces and soft hyphens, removes stray BOM markers, and can collapse extra runs of spaces and blank lines to a single canonical form that pastes cleanly into code and CMS editors.

faqs.q: Is there a way to sort and deduplicate a long list of lines?
faqs.a: Yes. The format module has sort ascending/descending, sort ignoring case, remove duplicates, remove blank lines, and reverse order. You can chain them — for example dedupe → sort ascending → normalize spacing — then copy the final list in one click.

timestamp-converter.name: Timestamp Converter
timestamp-converter.description: Online timestamp converter, bidirectional conversion between Unix timestamp and readable date, support ms/s/ISO formats, multi-timezone switch.

seo.intro: This Unix timestamp converter turns epoch timestamps into human-readable dates and back again. Paste a timestamp in seconds or milliseconds and it shows the corresponding date and time; paste a date and it returns the epoch value. It handles time zones and auto-detects whether your input is in seconds or milliseconds, which makes it a fast helper when debugging logs, database records or API responses. Everything is computed instantly in your browser.
scenarios: Debug a log line or API response that stores time as a raw epoch number.
Verify a database datetime field by converting it to a readable date.
Convert a scheduled time across time zones when planning releases or meetings.
tutorial: Paste a Unix timestamp, or a date, into the input.
Confirm whether it is in seconds or milliseconds (auto-detected).
Pick the time zone you want the result shown in.
Copy the converted date or timestamp.
advantages: Auto-detects seconds vs milliseconds so you don't misread the value.
Supports multiple time zones for cross-region work.
Instant, client-side conversion with no server round trip.

faqs.q: How do I tell seconds from milliseconds?
faqs.a: A seconds timestamp is usually 10 digits, milliseconds is 13 digits. The tool auto-detects the length, but you can override it if your value is unusual.

faqs.q: Does it support time zones?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose the time zone for the output, and it accounts for the offset when converting between a timestamp and a date.

faqs.q: Can I convert many values at once?
faqs.a: You can convert values one at a time quickly; for bulk lists, paste and convert each line as needed.

faqs.q: Does it support ISO 8601 dates?
faqs.a: Yes, standard ISO 8601 date strings are recognised as input and can be converted to an epoch timestamp.

faqs.q: Is the result in local time or UTC?
faqs.a: It depends on the time zone you select. Choose UTC for a universal value, or your local zone for a local reading.

title-weight-checker.name: Multi-Platform Title Weight Checker
title-weight-checker.description: Built-in 4-platform keyword banks (Xiaohongshu/Douyin/Video accounts/WeChat Official). Score per platform, detect banned words, chars limits, newline...

seo.intro: Multi-Platform Title Weight Checker is a free browser tool for operators and creators on Xiaohongshu (RED), Douyin / WeChat Video Channels, WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, Bilibili columns, YouTube, and Instagram. Paste a title or short-video cover headline, and it scores it against each platform's distinct sensitive-word, boost-word, and cold-start rules, highlighting risky / low-weight dead words and high-weight recommended hits so you can tune the title before publishing for better pass rates and algorithmic love.
scenarios: A Xiaohongshu beauty blogger writes 3 draft product-review titles, runs all three against the 'Xiaohongshu' channel, and picks the highest score — fewest absolute-risk deductions ('best', '#1', medical-claim adjacent words) plus the most hits on platform-favorite boost words like 'tried myself', 'budget', 'student friendly', 'warm + dark skin tones'

A Douyin short-video operator's draft title is stuffed with clickbait like 'MUST save this' and 'you will REGRET not watching'. Run the Douyin weight check first, swap the de-boosted / risk-of-review words for natural alternatives, and avoid the common 10-minute post-death where the platform throttles a video for low-quality headline

A Zhihu Q&A or WeChat long-form writer pastes a 20–35 character long-title and runs 'Zhihu' or 'WeChat Official' scoring, checking for cold-start-favor keywords (methodology, mistakes I made, year 202X, complete guide, step-by-step) and avoiding headline-party triggers that hurt WeChat originality checks.
tutorial: Type the title or main cover copy into the top input box. Recommend keeping length between roughly 6–40 Chinese characters or 5–15 English words: too short has no signal, too long gets truncated by every platform.

Choose the target platform: Xiaohongshu, Douyin / Video Channels, Zhihu, WeChat OA, Bilibili, YouTube, Instagram. Rules vary hugely (Xiaohongshu loves product-trial words, Zhihu loves methodology words) so pick the right channel.
Read three core outputs: total score 0–100 (higher is better), green-highlight high-weight boost hits, red-highlight risky / absolute words with per-word deduction reasons.

Copy the optimization suggestions. Replace red risk words with the platform-specific 'soft landing' synonyms shown, naturally sprinkle high-weight words near the front or end of the title, and re-score. A two-column A/B mode lets you compare versions side by side.
advantages: Covers 7+ mainstream creator platforms both inside and outside China (RED/Xiaohongshu, Douyin/WeChat Channels, Zhihu, WeChat OA, Bilibili, YouTube, Instagram). Per-platform boost word libraries sync quarterly, so one input can score cross-platform without you guessing rules on each site.

Three signal classes: high-weight boost words (score up), dead weight / marketing fluff words (score down), and platform-sensitive / absolute expressions (deduct and suggest safe replacements). Not a basic swear-word filter — it actually scores toward recommendation-friendly territory.

Side-by-side A/B two-column view highlights diffs in real time. Great for showing a boss or client why the optimized B version beats the original A version with concrete weight changes instead of subjective taste.

faqs.q: Does it suggest replacement words for risky tokens?
faqs.a: Yes. Every risky or dead-weight token shows 2–4 platform-appropriate soft-landing synonyms right underneath. For example, on Xiaohongshu 'most recommended' suggests 'tried and loved' or 'my current favorite'; on Douyin 'you MUST' suggests softer, natural high-CTR phrases that still drive clicks without sounding like clickbait.

faqs.q: Is weight score 1:1 with real platform traffic?
faqs.a: No. Title weight is only one input to the recommendation algorithm, next to first-second retention, cover CTR, comment engagement, and hundreds more signals. The tool guarantees you don't do dumb things — step over red lines that de-boost or garbage-filter your title — and nudges you toward words each platform prefers. A 90-point title does NOT guarantee 100k views.

faqs.q: Do my titles get uploaded to train any recommendation model?
faqs.a: Never. All matching runs locally in-browser via regex + dictionary lookups. Zero backend API calls, nothing is sent to any service. Feel safe to test commercial product copy, ad landing titles, even unreleased new-product headlines — nobody can see them.

faqs.q: What title length is best? Does it support English?
faqs.a: For Chinese, 6–40 characters is the sweet spot: below 6 there's not enough signal for stable scoring; above 40 every platform truncates. English titles (YouTube / Instagram) are fully supported, with a separate English-language power-word library including high-CTR terms (Ultimate, 2026, Hack, etc.).

faqs.q: Can I batch-score dozens or hundreds of titles?
faqs.a: Current version focuses on the single-title + two-column A/B compare experience, no real queue batching. That said, multi-line paste from an Excel column works fine in continuous mode — just step through row by row; it's still fast. If you need reports you can copy each result line into a sheet for aggregation.

url-encode-decode.name: URL Encode/Decode
url-encode-decode.description: Online URL encode/decode tool, standard percent-encoding, also supports Base64 encode/decode and HTML entity conversion.

seo.intro: This URL encoder and decoder converts text to and from percent-encoding (URL encoding) directly in your browser. Encode query parameters that contain spaces, non-ASCII characters or reserved symbols so they travel safely in a URL, or decode a %XX-escaped string back to readable text. It distinguishes the two common needs — encoding a whole URL versus encoding a single component — which mirrors JavaScript's encodeURI and encodeURIComponent. All processing is local, nothing is uploaded.
scenarios: Build a query string with values that contain spaces or Chinese characters.
Debug a redirect or callback URL that isn't matching because of encoding.
Decode a %XX-escaped string copied from a log or address bar to read it.
tutorial: Paste the URL or the parameter value.
Choose encode or decode.
Pick whole-URL mode or single-component mode.
Copy the result.
advantages: Separates full-URL and component encoding to avoid over- or under-escaping.
Handles non-ASCII input correctly.
Instant, local conversion with no server call.

faqs.q: What's the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faqs.a: encodeURI keeps URL structure characters like : / ? & intact, so it's for a full URL. encodeURIComponent escapes those too, so it's for a single value you'll insert into a URL.

faqs.q: Is a space encoded as %20 or +?
faqs.a: Percent-encoding uses %20. The + form is specific to application/x-www-form-urlencoded form data, not general URL encoding.

faqs.q: Does it support non-ASCII characters?
faqs.a: Yes. Characters such as Chinese are encoded as UTF-8 percent sequences and decoded back correctly.

faqs.q: Can I process multiple values?
faqs.a: Yes, encode or decode values one at a time; paste each string and convert as needed.

faqs.q: Will it change my original text?
faqs.a: Only by applying the encoding or decoding you choose. Decoding an already-decoded string, or encoding twice, can produce unexpected results, so apply the operation once.

uuid-generator.name: UUID Generator
uuid-generator.description: Generate UUIDs online, support v1/v4/v7, batch generate, one-click copy, pure local processing.

seo.intro: This UUID generator creates version 4 (random) UUIDs — also called GUIDs — instantly in your browser. Generate one or many at once, with or without hyphens, and in upper or lower case. UUIDs are 128-bit identifiers used as database keys, request IDs and unique references where a central counter isn't practical. Generation happens locally, so the values are produced on your device and not fetched from a server.
scenarios: Batch-generate UUIDs to seed database primary keys during development.
Create unique identifiers for test data or fixtures.
Produce an idempotency key or request ID for an API call.
tutorial: Choose the version (v4 random is the common default).
Set how many UUIDs you need.
Pick the format: with or without hyphens, upper or lower case.
Generate and copy them in bulk.
advantages: Generates in bulk, not one at a time.
Flexible formatting: hyphens and letter case options.
Produced locally in your browser — nothing is requested from a server.

faqs.q: What is the difference between v4 and v1?
faqs.a: v4 UUIDs are random, offering privacy and simplicity. v1 UUIDs are based on timestamp and machine info, which makes them time-ordered but can leak generation time and host.

faqs.q: Can UUIDs collide?
faqs.a: In theory yes, but the probability for v4 is astronomically small — you'd need to generate billions before a collision becomes remotely likely.

faqs.q: How many can I generate at once?
faqs.a: You can request many in a single batch; the practical limit depends on your browser's memory since generation is local.

faqs.q: Can I remove the hyphens?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose the no-hyphen format to get a compact 32-character string, useful for some database or URL contexts.

faqs.q: Are v4 UUIDs good as database primary keys?
faqs.a: They work well for distributed systems, but being random they can fragment index locality. If insert order matters, consider a time-ordered scheme instead.

vertical-chinese-generator.name: Vertical Chinese Vertical Layout Generator
vertical-chinese-generator.description: Traditional right-to-left vertical Chinese. Custom spacing/font size/flower decorative symbols. Xiaohongshu Guofeng cover notes. Export pure text +...

seo.intro: Vertical Chinese Text Generator is a free in-browser layout tool for Xiaohongshu creators, classical-Chinese poster designers, Hanfu photographers, guofeng cultural-goods makers, and calligraphy enthusiasts. Paste horizontal Chinese text (classical poetry, song lyrics, quotations, product titles, verses), choose vertical direction (right-to-left traditional / left-to-right modern), column dividers, punctuation position (trailing / cell-top), line spacing, number of columns, and whether to keep English / digits in horizontal mixed-layout (half-width chars auto-rotated 90°). The tool instantly renders copyable vertical rich text / image / SVG to paste straight into Xiaohongshu notes, ancient-style poster PSDs, Hanfu shoot captions, or guofeng cultural materials — no more laying out each character by hand column-by-column in Photoshop.
scenarios: A Xiaohongshu blogger posts a Dragon Boat poetry + Hanfu photoshoot guofeng note. Pastes a 4-line, 28-character seven-character quatrain, picks 'right-to-left 4 columns + dashed column dividers + regular script font + light vermilion text color', exports a 3:4 vertical image as cover — cover clicks were 2× higher than plain horizontal copy

A guofeng cultural-goods designer drafts 10 round-fan inscriptions for an offline craft market, 7–14 characters each. Runs the Vertical Generator once to produce 10 SVG vector files, drops them into Illustrator / Photoshop to tweak weight and color for final artwork — saves 3 hours of manual layout work

A Hanfu photographer's client wants a classical caption & seal on finished photos. Pastes the client's 16-character quotation, picks right-to-left 2 columns + thin Song font + seal-stamp placeholder, exports PNG and layers it onto the photo corner — delivered straight to the client, no need to fiddle with vertical direction in Photoshop.
tutorial: Paste horizontal text into the input: classical poems, quotes, modern prose, mixed Chinese-English phrases, numeric dates. Punctuation, emoji, spaces, and line breaks all preserve.

Pick layout parameters: vertical direction (right-to-left ancient tradition / left-to-right modern reading order), max characters per column (column count auto-calculated), column spacing, line spacing, column dividers (solid / dashed / none), font (Kai / Song / Hei / custom system fonts), text and background colors, border / padding.

Toggle mixed-layout rules: whether to auto-rotate English & Arabic numerals 90° for horizontal display (ancient-book standard), whether punctuation sits in the top-right of a character cell (trailing to a line) or bottom-left in its own cell, how half-width numeric dates occupy cells.

Choose export format: Copy Rich Text (pastes directly into Xiaohongshu / WeChat editors, preserving vertical direction and columns), export PNG with transparent background / JPG with background / SVG vector (ideal for further editing in PS / Illustrator), or pick preset sizes: 3:4 Xiaohongshu cover / 1:1 Moments square / 9:16 phone wallpaper.
advantages: True vertical layout, not just a CSS rotation: every character occupies its real grid cell aligned along the column direction per Unicode vertical-properties. 90° rotated English & digits follow real mixed-layout conventions, not the fake vertical of rotating a whole horizontal block 90° forcing people to tilt their heads.

All common poster / note size presets included: Xiaohongshu 3:4 vertical cover, Moments 1:1 square, the popular 4:5 aspect ratio for Hanfu photoshoots, 9:16 phone wallpaper — no need to look up dimensions and create a new canvas manually.

100% browser-local rendering, zero upload. Client-confidential classical slogans, commercial poster copy, copyrighted poetry layouts all paste safely. SVG / PNG exports are generated entirely locally via Canvas + SVG in the browser, no backend storage whatsoever.

faqs.q: Is the exported PNG transparent? Can I drag it straight into Photoshop onto a photo layer?
faqs.a: Default PNG export has a transparent background. When you leave background color empty the PNG carries an alpha channel, so it drops straight into Photoshop / CapCut / Xingtu as an overlay layer with no solid white box. If you pick a background color it will export with one, both modes are switchable in export options.

faqs.q: Can I use custom fonts? I have my own Kai-style OTF font file to use.
faqs.a: Two ways: ① any font already installed on your system shows up directly in the dropdown (Source Han Serif / Hanyi Kai etc. if installed pick directly); ② the tool also supports browser-local import of TTF / OTF / WOFF2 files — just drag the font file onto the font area and it works instantly, no upload, the file is parsed entirely inside the browser.

faqs.q: What's the difference between right-to-left and left-to-right vertical? Which should I pick?
faqs.a: Right-to-left is the authentic reading order of classical Chinese books, calligraphy, and traditional posters — pick this for the most formal guofeng / ancient aesthetic. Left-to-right is the vertical layout order used in some modern vertically-typeset publications (e.g. some Taiwan editions), good for modern literary captions where contemporary reading comfort matters more. Pick whichever matches your overall content style.

faqs.q: Punctuation placement looks wrong? Sometimes a '。' sits in the middle of a character.
faqs.a: Switch the punctuation layout mode before export: 'Trailing (classical standard)' puts periods and commas in the top-right of the character cell (used in calligraphy / ancient books), 'Own cell (publishing standard)' gives punctuation its own cell in the bottom-left (modern book publishing standard). Flipping between these fixes punctuation placement, and advanced options let you individually tune exclamation / question mark cell behavior too.

faqs.q: Mixed English & digits look crooked?
faqs.a: Turn on the 'English / digits auto-horizontal' toggle. The tool auto-detects runs of English words and Arabic numerals, rotates them 90° to display horizontally inside the vertical layout (per classical mixed-layout rules), instead of stacking each letter individually top-to-bottom — so you don't have to tilt your head to read them. If you do want each letter stacked vertically (decorative calligraphy use), just turn the toggle off.

wallpaper-maker.name: Phone Wallpaper Studio
wallpaper-maker.description: Create custom phone wallpapers from gradients + text. 16 gradient presets, customizable text, font and size. One-click export.

seo.intro: Phone Wallpaper Studio is a free browser-based wallpaper maker that combines custom gradients, solid colors, emoji stickers, and editable text overlays into high-resolution phone wallpapers sized for any modern iPhone or Android lock/home screen. Choose from preset gradient palettes, drag text or emoji anywhere on the canvas, and export as a crisp PNG that fits the exact aspect ratio you select. All rendering happens on-device in pure Canvas — no image uploads, no background API calls, and no watermarks on the final file.
scenarios: Making a custom gradient lock-screen wallpaper with a personal motto or date in under 30 seconds for a new phone setup
Creating brand-colored team wallpapers with a logo emoji and company slogan so every teammate can apply a consistent home-screen look
Generating matching aesthetic pastel wallpapers with a favorite emoji or quote for a Xiaohongshu or Pinterest share-worthy setup
tutorial: Select your target device aspect ratio or type a custom resolution in pixels
Pick a base layer: solid color, two-tone linear gradient, or radial gradient from the preset palette
Click to add text overlays (with font, size, and color controls) and drag emoji stickers anywhere on the canvas
Preview the result and export as a PNG file, then Airdrop / send the file to your phone to set as wallpaper
advantages: Zero-upload pure Canvas rendering, so personal text, private dates, and custom slogans never leave the browser for any server-side processing
Device presets cover iPhone 14–17, Samsung Galaxy, Pixel, and generic 1080x1920 / 1440x3200 ratios so there's no guesswork on sizing
Unlimited re-edits before export: reposition text, swap palettes, add or remove stickers without losing quality thanks to vector canvas rendering

faqs.q: Do I need to upload a background photo or register to make a wallpaper?
faqs.a: No. The tool builds wallpapers entirely from gradients, solid colors, sticker shapes, and text you type — no photo upload and no account. Everything renders locally in your browser via HTML5 Canvas, so the final PNG is generated right on your machine.

faqs.q: Which phone sizes and aspect ratios are supported?
faqs.a: Presets include iPhone (1176×2556, 1290×2796, etc.), Samsung/Google flagships, and generic 9:16/20:9 ratios. You can also type any custom width/height in pixels for tablets, foldables, or desktop wallpaper use cases.

faqs.q: Can I add my own text and change fonts on the wallpaper?
faqs.a: Yes. The text overlay tool lets you pick from dozens of fonts, adjust size, weight, color, opacity, and text-shadow, and drag the result anywhere on the canvas. Multi-line text is supported so long quotes or date+name combos render cleanly.

faqs.q: Does the exported PNG contain a watermark?
faqs.a: No. Every exported wallpaper is a clean, high-resolution PNG with no site watermark, no logo overlay, and no metadata tracking. You can freely share the result on social or print it without attribution requirements.

faqs.q: Can I save a draft and come back to edit it later?
faqs.a: The current version stores your last wallpaper state in the page session so you can tweak colors or text within the same tab. For longer-term saves, we recommend exporting the PNG once you're happy — re-import and overlay additional elements with the same tool if you want to iterate later.
